title: Phase 1: collect, store and show statistics
body:
## What

Phase 1 of `todo/PLANS.md`: collect, store and show site statistics. Design: `docs/architecture.md`.

## Steps (each a PR or part of one)

- [ ] Architecture, plan and agent guide (`docs/architecture.md`, `todo/PLANS.md`, `AGENTS.md`)

- [ ] Tracker (`packages/tracker`), printed inline on front-end pages; needs the starter's JavaScript build support
- [ ] Processor: user agents, channels, location, sessions, facts; cron; nightly summaries; retention
- [ ] Report engine, REST API, OpenAPI file, WP-CLI

Each step: `scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/smoke-test.sh` on WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4 and latest / PHP 8.3, and the preview site (`scripts/preview-site.sh`): hits from logged-out front-end visits reach the buffer, then the tables, then the dashboard.

title: Overview polish: Events card, <0.1% shares, partial today; longer retention
body:
## What

Phase 1 follow-ups from preview review:

1. **Retention defaults:** visits and pageviews kept 75 months (was 13), events and revenue 120 months (was 25). Daily summaries are still kept forever.
2. **Events card on the Overview:** top events by count, with the share of visits that had each event (its conversion rate); choosing a row filters the view to visits with that event.
3. **Tiny shares:** a share above zero that would round to 0% reads `<0.1%`.
4. **Partial period on the chart:** the point still being counted (today, this hour, this month) is drawn dotted with a lighter fill and labelled "(so far)" in the tooltip and the screen-reader table, so a low number reads as unfinished, not a drop.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostats-statistics.php` (`retention_visits`, `retention_events` defaults and descriptions), `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-rollup.php` (`RETENTION` fallback), `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-cli.php` (prune docblock), `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md` (Retention table).
- `packages/core/src/format.ts` (`formatPercent`).
- `packages/charts/src/timeseries.ts` (`ChartSeries.partialFrom`: the series is drawn as a solid line plus a dotted tail).
- `packages/wp-admin/src/components/MainChart.tsx` (`partialIndex()`: the point whose period holds the answer's `generated` time), `packages/wp-admin/src/components/BreakdownCard.tsx` (count by dimension, `wide`), `packages/wp-admin/src/Overview.tsx`, `packages/wp-admin/src/dashboard.css`.

## Verification

`scripts/lint.sh`; `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`; the preview site: Overview shows the Events card and today dotted; Settings → Data shows 75 and 120 on an install that never saved them; `wp seoprostats prune --dry-run`.

Existing installs that saved the Data tab keep their saved months; installs that never saved them get the new defaults.

title: Dashboard widget: start at the top of the right-most column; fit SEO Pro Stack's tidy Dashboard
body:
## What

The Dashboard widget should start at the top of the right-most column for the person's column count, and fit SEO Pro Stack's tidy Dashboard.

WordPress shows one to four Dashboard columns by screen width and the Layout screen option, laid out with floats (`wp-admin/css/dashboard.css`), so no single registered context is top-right at every width.

## How

- `includes/admin/class-seoprostats-dashboard.php`: register the widget in `side` with `high` priority (the top of the right-hand column in WordPress's usual two); pass `placeWidget` in the widget's boot data when no saved `meta-box-order_dashboard` includes the widget; add a `seoprostack_dashboard_layout` filter that puts it at the top of SEO Pro Stack's `column3` (visitors and SEO) unless the rules already place it. Same pattern as the existing `menu_catalog()` for `seoprostack_admin_menu_catalog`.
- `packages/wp-admin/src/placeWidget.ts` (new): measure the visible `.postbox-container`s, take those reaching the far side (right; left in RTL), and put the widget at the top of the topmost; again on resize and on a Layout screen option change; stop on core's `postbox-moved` event, after which WordPress saves the person's arrangement.
- Docs: `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md` (Dashboard screen and widget).

## Verification

`scripts/lint.sh`; `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`; the preview site at 1, 2, 3 and 4 columns (widths 700, 1280, 1600, 1920) with SEO Pro Stack's tidy Dashboard off, and with it on.

title: Demo data: a Live/Demo switch with made-up visits in tables of their own
body:
## What

A **Demo data** switch on the Overview that swaps live statistics for made-up visits, for training, screenshots and testing. Demo data lives in tables of its own with the same layout, so the two never mix and reports use the same code and queries for both.

## How

- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php`: a data set (`use_set('live'|'demo')`, `set()`, `SETS`); `table()` gives `seoprostats_demo_*` names for demo; `option()` gives the per-set option names (table version, processing and summary progress) with `_demo` after the live name; `install()`, `is_current()` and `drop()` work on the current set.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-demo.php` (new): makes visits as the collector writes them (real user agents, referrers, UTM tags, click IDs, countries, languages, events with properties, purchases with revenue) and passes them to `SEOProStats_Processor::ingest()`, then the daily summaries; 400 days by default, in slices of up to ten seconds, with an option lock; tops up to the present while shown; `remove()` drops the demo tables and options.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-processor.php`: `ingest()` runs lines that did not come through the buffer through the same batch code.
- `class-seoprostats-query.php`, `class-seoprostats-rollup.php`, `class-seoprostats-dict.php`: caches and progress per data set; demo has no buffer, so `Rollup::clear()` is now.
- `class-seoprostats-api.php`: `data=live|demo` on the report routes (404 when there is no demo data); `GET|POST|DELETE /demo`; `POST /view` (user meta `seoprostats_data`).
- `class-seoprostats-cli.php`: `--data=demo` on reports; `wp seoprostats demo make|status|remove`.
- Dashboard app: `data.ts` store, `components/Demo.tsx` (switch and notice, making it with progress for administrators), report queries keyed by data set; the Dashboard widget follows the choice and says when it shows demo data.
- `uninstall.php`: removes the demo tables, options and user meta.
- Docs: `docs/architecture.md` (Storage → Demo data, Interfaces), `docs/api/openapi.yaml`.

## Verification

`scripts/lint.sh`; `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`; on the preview site: make demo data from the screen and with WP-CLI, check live numbers are unchanged, compare demo reports on summarised days and fact tables, switch back and forth on the Overview and the Dashboard widget, remove it.

title: Goals, funnels and properties: definitions, reports, REST, WP-CLI and dashboard sections
body:
## What

Phase 2 of the plan (`todo/PLANS.md`): conversions.

- **Goals**: a page viewed or an event sent (`*` for any text) counts as a conversion. Report: visitors, visits that converted, completions, conversion rate and revenue per currency, compared with the other period.
- **Funnels**: 2 to 12 ordered steps within one visit (other hits may come between). Report: visits at each step, share of those that started, drop-off from the step before.
- **Properties**: the keys sent with events and pages, and one key's values with visits, share and revenue; optionally of one event.
- Goals and funnels are per data set: live and demo each keep their own; demo data comes with examples.
- REST: `GET /goals`, `GET /funnels`, `GET /properties`; administrators `POST /goals`, `POST|PUT|DELETE /goals/{id}` and the same for funnels. WP-CLI: `wp seoprostats goals|funnels|properties`.
- wp-admin: Overview, Goals, Funnels and Properties sections (tabs and menu items) with goal and funnel editors.
- Also: a second click on a row that is already a filter removes it; space under the demo notices.

## Files

- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-goals.php`, `class-seoprostats-conversions.php` (new); `class-seoprostats-api.php`, `class-seoprostats-cli.php`, `class-seoprostats-demo.php`, `class-seoprostats-query.php`, `includes/admin/class-seoprostats-dashboard.php`, `uninstall.php`

title: feat: click and form autocapture, dead clicks, affiliate links, Clicks section
body:
## What

Phase 2 of the plan (`todo/PLANS.md`): clicks and forms.

- **Autocapture** in the tracker: clicks on links, buttons and other things that look clickable (`cursor: pointer`, images), and form submits. Each sends the element as `tag#id.class`, its visible label (60 characters), the link's destination (origin and path; `mailto:`/`tel:` without the address) and flags. Form submits send the form's name and field count. Never field values; emails and long numbers in labels are masked; `data-sps-mask` hides an element's label.
- **Dead clicks**: a click on something clickable with no reaction (DOM change, navigation, scroll or focus change) within one second.
- **Outbound, affiliate and download** flags. Affiliate links are links to the site's own cloaked paths (Settings → Tracking, default `/go/*` and `/recommends/*`) or links with `rel="sponsored"`; they send an **Affiliate link** event (instead of no event), so a goal can count them.
- **Storage**: a `clicks` table (schema v4) joined to its page load, so clicks never start or extend visits or change `seq`. Kept 3 months (Settings → Data), pruned with the rest.
- **Report**: `GET /clicks` (`kind`: elements, dead, links, downloads, forms) with totals, and `wp seoprostats clicks`. Page and visit filters apply.
- **wp-admin**: a Clicks section (tab and menu item) with totals, a kind switch and a page field.
- Demo data gets clicks, dead clicks, affiliate links and form submits.
- Settings: switch autocapture off; affiliate link paths; months to keep clicks.

## Files

- `packages/tracker/src/index.ts`; `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-tracker.php` (config)
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-processor.php`, `class-seoprostats-schema.php`, `class-seoprostats-rollup.php` (retention), `class-seoprostats-demo.php`
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-clicks.php` (new report), `class-seoprostats-api.php`, `class-seoprostats-cli.php`
- `includes/features/class-seoprostats-statistics.php` (settings), `includes/admin/class-seoprostats-dashboard.php` (menu item)
- `packages/core/src/{types,state}.ts`, `packages/wp-admin/src/{App,Clicks,api}.tsx|ts`, `dashboard.css`
- `docs/api/openapi.yaml`, `docs/architecture.md`, `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, `todo/PLANS.md`

## Check

- `scripts/lint.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4` pass; the tracker stays small (size in the PR).
- In a browser on the preview: clicks, a dead click, an outbound and an affiliate link and a form submit arrive and show in the Clicks section; no field value is stored.
- With demo data: the report answers by REST, WP-CLI and in wp-admin; its queries use indexes (`EXPLAIN`); retention removes old clicks.

title: feat: keep each section's choices in the view address, ready for shared views
body:
## What

Every choice made inside a section belongs in the view address (URL hash), like the period, comparison and filters already are, so a bookmark, the back button or a copied address brings back exactly the same view. Today these are React state and are lost on reload:

- **Clicks**: the kind (`elements`, `dead`, `links`, `downloads`, `forms`) and the page field (`packages/wp-admin/src/Clicks.tsx:114-115`).
- **Properties**: the chosen key and event (`packages/wp-admin/src/Properties.tsx:22-23`).
- **Overview**: the open tab of each breakdown card: Sources, Pages, Locations, Devices (`packages/wp-admin/src/components/BreakdownCard.tsx:125`; cards made in `Overview.tsx:56-101`).

Text typed in a field is not view state until it is applied (Apply or Enter).

### Ready for shared views

Phase 6 of `todo/PLANS.md` adds shared read-only dashboards (a private link, like a post preview link, with optional password and expiry) so a site owner can give a client a live view of the reports that matter to them without a WordPress account. A share will store a view, so build this change as that view's format:

- **One serialisable object.** All view state stays in `ViewState` in `packages/core/src/state.ts`, with pure `parseHash()` / `buildHash()` (no WordPress or React, so later apps reuse them and the server can validate a stored view). Section-specific values go in the same object, for example an optional `kind`, `page`, `key`, `event` and a `tabs` map keyed by card (`sources`, `pages`, `locations`, `devices`), whichever reads most simply.
- **Strict and tolerant.** Every value is checked against its list or pattern; anything unknown or invalid falls back to the default, and defaults are left out of the address, so old bookmarks keep working and addresses stay short.
- **Nothing private in it.** No user IDs, nonces or settings; only what is needed to draw the view. The Live/Demo data switch stays a per-user setting, outside the address (a shared view always shows live data).
- **Section values belong to their section.** Switching section keeps the shared values (period, comparison, filters, metric) and drops the other section's values.

Sharing itself (tokens, the public screen, permissions) is not part of this issue.

## Files

- `packages/core/src/state.ts`: `ViewState`, `DEFAULT_STATE`, `parseHash()`, `buildHash()`.
- `packages/wp-admin/src/hash.ts` (`useViewState`), `App.tsx` (section links via `buildHash`).
- `packages/wp-admin/src/Clicks.tsx`, `Properties.tsx`, `Overview.tsx`, `components/BreakdownCard.tsx`: read and write the values through `state` / `update` instead of `useState`.
- `docs/architecture.md` → Dashboard (the paragraph on the URL hash, around line 494): list what the address holds and the shared-view constraint; `changelog.txt` (one line).

Reference pattern: `metric` and `filters` in `state.ts` (validated with `oneOf()`, omitted when default).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `packages/core/src/state.ts`
- EDIT: `packages/wp-admin/src/hash.ts`
- EDIT: `packages/wp-admin/src/App.tsx`
- EDIT: `packages/wp-admin/src/Clicks.tsx`
- EDIT: `packages/wp-admin/src/Properties.tsx`
- EDIT: `packages/wp-admin/src/Overview.tsx`
- EDIT: `packages/wp-admin/src/components/BreakdownCard.tsx`
- EDIT: `assets/build/dashboard.js`
- EDIT: `assets/build/dashboard.asset.php`
- EDIT: `docs/architecture.md`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`

## Check

- `composer install && scripts/lint.sh` passes (includes `npm run check`); `scripts/smoke-test.sh` is not needed unless PHP changes.
- In a browser on the preview (`scripts/preview-site.sh`): choose a Clicks kind and a page, a Properties key and event, and a non-default tab on each Overview card; reload and open the copied address in a new tab: the same view each time. The back button steps back through the choices. Change section and come back: the period and filters are kept, the other section's values are not carried across.
- Hand-edit the address with an unknown kind, tab or key: the view opens with defaults and no console errors. An address from before this change opens as before.

title: feat: Clicks by page, with View and Edit links for the page
body:
## What

The Clicks section (issue #22, PR #23) says what was clicked but not where, unless the reader types a page. Add the page level, not a page per row: an element row adds up every page it was clicked on (a menu link is on every page), so a page link per row would mislead and crowd the table.

- **A Pages kind**: `pages` joins `SEOProStats_Clicks::KINDS`: one row per page with clicks, dead clicks, dead-click rate, link clicks, forms sent and visits, sorted by clicks (a sort by dead clicks is a nice extra, not required). It answers "where do people get stuck". Grouped by `clicks.path_id`, which the `path_ts (path_id, ts)` key already covers; no schema change.
- **Choosing a page row** narrows the section to that page (sets the page field), and choosing it again clears it, the same toggle the other reports use.
- **View and Edit links** when the section is narrowed to one exact page (not a `*` pattern): the header shows the page with **View page** (opens the address on the site in a new tab) and **Edit** (the post editor) links. The REST answer gets `page_info: {path, url, post_id, edit_url}`, resolved on the server with `url_to_postid()`; `edit_url` only when `current_user_can('edit_post', $post_id)`, otherwise null. Never on visitor pages (this is an admin REST request). Shared read-only views (Phase 6) must leave `edit_url` out; keep it a separate field so they can.
- The `pages` rows may carry the same `url` (and `edit_url` for at most the rows shown) so each row can offer small View and Edit icons; resolve only the rows returned (limit 10 by default), inside the report cache.
- **WP-CLI**: `wp seoprostats clicks pages`; the page line prints the post ID and edit address when known.
- **Demo data**: demo paths may not match posts on the site; `edit_url` is then null and only View shows.

Keep each link a real `<a>` with an accessible name (for example "View /pricing/ (opens in a new tab)"), WordPress's own link and icon styles, and the admin colour scheme.

## Files

- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-clicks.php`: `pages` kind, `page_info`.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-api.php`: the `kind` enum takes `pages`.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-cli.php`: `clicks pages`, page line.
- `packages/core/src/types.ts`: `CLICK_KINDS`, row and answer types.
- `packages/wp-admin/src/Clicks.tsx` (tile or switch for Pages, header links, row toggle), `dashboard.css` if needed; rebuilt `assets/build/`.
- `docs/api/openapi.yaml` (`/clicks` kind, `page_info`), `docs/architecture.md` (Clicks report), `README.md`, `changelog.txt`.

Reference pattern: the elements/dead/links rows in `SEOProStats_Clicks::rows()` and row-click filters in `packages/wp-admin/src/components/BreakdownCard.tsx`.

## What

Shared reports: a private link, like a post preview link, that opens a live, interactive, read-only report for someone without a WordPress account, typically an agency's or freelancer's client who wants a monitoring dashboard of what matters to them. Phase 6 of `todo/PLANS.md` ("Shared read-only dashboards (private link, password, expiry)"); `docs/architecture.md` already keeps share tokens as small option arrays with autoload off.

Builds on issue #24: a view is one `ViewState` (`packages/core/src/state.ts`), so a share stores views in that format and the server validates them with the same rules.

### What the owner sets up (wp-admin, administrators)

- **A Shared reports screen** (a section and menu item, or a tab in Settings; whichever fits the menu better): a list of shares with name, sections, created, expires, last opened, opens count, and Copy link, Edit, Revoke, Make a new link.
- **Make one from where you are**: a **Share** button beside the period controls saves the current view (section, period, comparison, filters, tabs) as the start of a new share.
- **What it shows**: one or more sections or cards in order (for example Overview, Goals and Clicks), each a saved view. Later sections (Rankings, Changes, Speed and so on) become shareable by joining an allow list, with no change to the format.
- **What viewers may change**: period (any, or within a maximum such as the last 12 months), comparison, choosing rows to filter, switching tabs. **Locked filters** the viewer cannot remove: a share for one campaign, one folder (`/shop/*`) or one country shows only that, on every report and chart, enforced on the server.
- **Access**: optional password; optional expiry date; revoke at any time; Make a new link (old link stops). Optionally "hide the realtime visitor count" and "hide search terms and referrer addresses" for shares to people outside the business.
- **A note for the reader**: optional text at the top ("Monthly results for Acme: the campaign started on 3 March"), and the change markers lane on charts (Phase 3) when it exists, so the cause and effect the plugin is about reach the client too.

### Branding

- **Site header**: the site's logo (Customizer logo, else Site Icon, else none) and the site name, linked to the home page; a share may use its own logo and title instead.
- **Agency footer** (optional): the agency's logo (Media Library), name, website link and byline, for example "Report prepared by Northwind Digital". Set once as defaults in Settings → Shared reports, overridable per share. Links are `rel="noopener"`; no third-party requests (logos are the site's own media).
- **Accent colour**: picked per share or from the defaults (used for the chart line, active tab and links), checked for contrast against the background; text never takes it below WCAG AA.
- **Light, dark or the viewer's system** setting, and a toggle on the page. The share page is the plugin's own screen, not themed, so it may use `prefers-color-scheme` for "system"; colours come from its own variables, never fixed per mode in components.
- A small "Statistics by SEO Pro Stats" credit, which the owner can switch off.
- Print styles, so "Print / Save as PDF" in the browser gives a clean report with the branding (scheduled email and PDF reports stay in "Alerts and email reports").

### How it works

- **Address**: `/?seoprostats_share=<token>` (works without permalinks), or a pretty `/statistics/<token>/` when permalinks are on. The rewrite rule check must cost nothing on other requests. Pages send `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: private, no-store`; never in sitemaps.
- **Token**: 128-bit random, shown once in full (copyable), stored only as a hash (like application passwords); compared in constant time. Password: `wp_hash_password()`; unlocking gives a short-lived signed token kept in `sessionStorage`, not a cookie. Throttle failed attempts per share.
- **Read-only REST**: `GET /share/{token}/…` routes (or the existing report routes with a share token header) that only answer the share's sections, apply its locked filters and period limits on the server, never reach goal or funnel editors, settings, demo data, users or edit links (issue #25's `edit_url` stays null), and use the existing report cache. Rate-limited per token.
- **The page**: the dashboard app's section components (`packages/wp-admin/src/`) rendered in a slim shell, a new `share` entry, without wp-admin. Shared views of the screen reader tables stay.
- **Viewers are not tracked**: the share page prints no tracker and is excluded from statistics.
- **Manage by REST and WP-CLI** (`manage_options`): `/shares` CRUD; `wp seoprostats share list|create|revoke|renew`. Abilities later.
- **Uninstall** removes shares and their options.

title: feat: not found pages, site search, content and logged-in visits
body:
## What

Phase 2 of the plan (`todo/PLANS.md`, "Enhanced"): what WordPress knows about a page, measured without extra cost on visitor pages. WooCommerce and Easy Digital Downloads purchases are a separate slice.

- **Not found**: page loads that answered 404, by address, with visits and where those visits came from, so broken links can be found and fixed.
- **Site search**: what people searched for on the site, how often, and which searches found nothing. Terms are cleaned like click labels (emails and long numbers masked, 100 characters); a setting (Settings → Tracking) switches term recording off.
- **Content**: views by author, category (the SEO plugin's primary category when set, else the first) and post type, for singular pages.
- **Logged in**: visits by people who were logged in (roles that are counted; roles that are not counted are still never tracked) against those who were not.

### How

- `SEOProStats_Tracker` prints the page's context in a `data-ctx` attribute: 404, search term and result count, post ID, type, author ID and category ID, logged in. Only from what the request has already loaded (the queried object, the main query's term and meta caches, `is_user_logged_in()`): no query, option or remote request on a visitor page (smoke test). The tracker sends it with the page load's first pageview only.
- The processor (cron) writes: `pageviews.flags` (1 not found, 2 site search, 4 no results) and `pageviews.search_id` (a dictionary text); `sessions.login` (0 or 1); and a `pages` row per address (`path_id`, `post_id`, `post_type`, `author_id`, `term_id`, `seen`), the start of the pages table in `docs/architecture.md` → Storage. Schema v5.
- Report dimensions for breakdowns and filters: `not_found`, `search`, `author`, `category`, `post_type` (page level) and `login` (visit level, in the daily summaries). Names (authors, categories, post types) are looked up when a report is made, in wp-admin or the API, never stored as text.
- REST and WP-CLI take the new dimensions (`breakdown --dimension=search`); the OpenAPI enum and TypeScript types follow.
- **Overview**: the Pages card gets a Not found tab; new cards Site search (Searches, No results) and Content (Authors, Categories, Post types); the Devices card gets a Logged in tab, or a card of its own if that reads better.
- **Demo data**: a few 404s (old addresses and typos), searches with some empty results, authors and categories for its posts, and some logged-in visits.

title: feat: A/B testing of blocks: variants in the editor, results grouped by test and variant
body:
## What

A/B testing of blocks: any block (or group of blocks) can have several variants, each anything the editor can make, and SEO Pro Stats shows which variant leads to more of what matters (goals, revenue, clicks, engagement), with everything that had a test grouped by test and variant in the reports. Private by design like the rest: no cookies, no browser storage by default, no third-party requests. Not in `todo/PLANS.md` yet; the purchases PR adds it as its own item.

### In the editor (block editor, wp-admin)

- **Start a test from any block**: a toolbar button on every block (and on a multi-block selection), "A/B test", wraps the selection in a test block (`seoprostats/ab-test`) whose children are variant blocks (`seoprostats/ab-variant`). Variant A is the original content; Variant B starts as a copy to change. Any block type inside works, including groups, columns, buttons, images and patterns, because a variant holds inner blocks.
- **Switch variants inline**: a dropdown in the test block's toolbar ("Variant A ▾") picks which variant is shown and edited in the canvas; the others are hidden in the editor, not removed. Keyboard reachable, labelled for screen readers.
- **Sidebar panel** (block settings) for the test block, with tabs or a list of variants:
  - Names: `variant-a`, `variant-b`, … by default (shown as "Variant A"), renamable; the slug stays stable once data exists, so renaming changes only the label.
  - Add (blank or duplicate of the current one), remove, reorder; traffic split (equal by default, weights per variant).
  - Test name (default from the post title and block), status (draft, running, paused, ended), and the goal(s) it is judged by (from Goals), shown with the results.
  - **Results in the sidebar** when the post has data: per variant views, conversion rate on the chosen goal and a short verdict ("B is ahead, 94% likely better", "too early"), linking to the full report.
  - **Pick a winner**: replaces the test block with the chosen variant's blocks (undoable), ends the test and keeps its results.
- A test has a stable random ID stored in its block attributes, so copying a post or moving the block keeps or renews it deliberately (duplicate IDs in one post are renewed on save).
- Site editor templates and synced patterns can come later; say so in the UI if the button is missing there.

### On the site

- The server prints the control (Variant A, or the winner) as normal markup and the other variants inside `<template>` elements, so crawlers, AI agents, no-JS visitors and feeds see one variant and no duplicate text, and page caches keep one copy.
- A tiny inline script printed right after the test block (or one shared script in the head stub) picks a variant by weight for that page load before paint and swaps the template in, so there is no flicker. No query, option read or remote request on a visitor page (the test's weights and status are in the block's own attributes).
- Paused, ended and draft tests print only the control (or the winner) and no script.
- **Assignment without identity**: by default a variant is chosen per page load, because the tracker stores nothing in the browser. A visit that saw more than one variant of the same test counts as "mixed" and is left out of the comparison (reported as a count). An opt-in setting (Settings → Tracking, off by default, explained as storage that privacy law treats like cookies) keeps one variant per visit with `sessionStorage`.
- The pageview sends which test and variant it showed (with the page load's ID, so clicks and events of that page load join it); clicks inside a variant carry the variant.

### In SEO Pro Stats

- **Experiments section** (tab and menu item under Behaviour): one row per test with its page, status, start and end, variants, visits per variant, and the leader. A test's view: per variant visits exposed, conversions and conversion rate for each chosen goal, revenue per currency (never added across currencies), bounce rate, engaged time, clicks; uplift against the control with an interval; probability to beat the control (Bayesian, beta-binomial for rates); a plain-language verdict with a "too early" state below a minimum sample; mixed visits counted apart.
- **Grouped where relevant**: a `variant` dimension (value `test-id:variant-slug`, label "Test name: Variant B") for filters and breakdowns, so every report (Overview, Goals, Funnels, Clicks, Properties) can be split or filtered by variant; Pages and page detail mark pages with a running test and link to it; the Clicks report on a page with a test can group clicks by variant; test start, pause, end and winner become change markers on the timeline (Phase 3 lane) when that exists.
- **REST and WP-CLI**: `GET /experiments`, `GET /experiments/{id}`; `wp seoprostats experiments [<id>]`; the OpenAPI spec and TypeScript types follow. Abilities later.
- **Demo data**: two or three example tests (a headline, a button, a pricing block) with a clear winner and one too-early test.

### How (suggested; the worker may refine)

- Storage: exposures per page load (`pageview_id`/`pkey`, test, variant) in a small table or as pageview properties, whichever keeps reports on indexes (`EXPLAIN`; `STANDARDS.md` → Performance). A test registry (ID, post, name, variants, status, goals, dates) written when a post is saved (`save_post`, parsing its blocks), never on visitor pages; names looked up when a report is made.
- Take the next free schema version at merge time (the purchases work may also change the schema).
- Editor code: a new editor script (block registration, the toolbar button via `editor.BlockEdit`/`BlockControls`, the sidebar via `InspectorControls`) as its own webpack entry, using `@wordpress/components`; front-end swap script under the 4 KB tracker budget or separate and tiny.

title: feat: purchases from WooCommerce, EDD, FluentCart and ThriveCart as revenue events
body:
## What

Purchases from WooCommerce, Easy Digital Downloads, FluentCart and ThriveCart become `Purchase` events with revenue in each order's currency, recorded once per order, on the server when the order is paid, and joined to the visit that checked out. Goals, funnels, revenue per currency and the REST API, WP-CLI and dashboard then show sales by source, page and campaign with no extra set-up. `todo/PLANS.md` Phase 2 → Purchases (it named WooCommerce and EDD; this adds FluentCart and ThriveCart).

## How

Private like the rest: no cookies, nothing stored in the browser, no visitor identity across days.

- **Shops on the site (WooCommerce, EDD, FluentCart).** When an order is placed in the customer's own checkout request, the plugin works out that request's visitor hash exactly as the collector does (`HMAC(daily salt, ip | user agent | host)`, `SEOProStats_Collector`), applying the same exclusions as the tracker (collection off, excluded roles, Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control when respected, excluded addresses), and keeps the hash, the time and the user agent in the order's meta. When the order is paid (on the spot or later by the gateway or an admin) one `Purchase` event line goes into the buffer with that hash and the checkout time, so the processor joins it to the visit as any other event; the meta is then replaced by a "recorded" mark, so a second paid hook does nothing. Orders made in wp-admin, by cron (subscription renewals) or by the REST API have no hash and are left out: they are not site visits.
  - WooCommerce (HPOS and posts): `woocommerce_checkout_order_processed`, `woocommerce_store_api_checkout_order_processed`; paid on `woocommerce_payment_complete`, `woocommerce_order_status_processing`, `woocommerce_order_status_completed`; `$order->get_total()`, `get_currency()`, order meta API.
  - EDD 3: `edd_built_order` (checkout); paid on `edd_complete_purchase`; `edd_get_order()`, `edd_*_order_meta()`.
  - FluentCart: `fluent_cart/order_created` (checkout API); paid on `fluent_cart/order_paid` (`['order' => Order]`); `total_amount` is in cents; `type` `renewal` skipped; `Order::getMeta()`/`updateMeta()`.
- **ThriveCart (checkout on thrivecart.com).** The tracker adds the page load's random ID as `passthrough[spst]` to ThriveCart checkout links when they are clicked (only when ThriveCart is connected). A webhook route, `POST /wp-json/seoprostats/v1/thrivecart` (HEAD/GET answer 200 for ThriveCart's URL check), checks the account's secret word (`thrivecart_secret`, compared with `hash_equals`), takes `order.success` (form encoded; `order.total` in cents, `currency`, `order_id`, `passthrough[spst]`), looks the page load up in `pageviews` by its unique `pkey`, and writes the event line with that visit's visitor hash and the page load's time. Each order is recorded once (recent order IDs kept in an option, autoload off). Orders without a known page load (embedded checkouts, links shared elsewhere) are counted in a "not joined" total, not invented as visits. The secret word is a setting under Settings → Tracking, with the webhook address to paste into ThriveCart.
- **Event.** Name `Purchase`, revenue `{amount, currency}` (amount in major units, as the tracker sends it), properties `source` (woocommerce, edd, fluentcart, thrivecart) and `items` (count). No order number, customer name, email or address is stored.
- **Processor.** Server lines are marked (`s: 1`): they skip the user-agent bot check (an empty or gateway user agent), and they never carry an IP prefix.
- **Unknown, to check while building:** ThriveCart's exact HEAD/response expectations and retries, whether `passthrough` arrives as `passthrough[spst]` or nested, and whether bump and upsell totals are in `order.total`; WooCommerce block checkout's request is the visitor's own (IP and user agent); FluentCart's checkout request path.
- Refunds and subscription renewals are out of scope here (follow-up).

## Files

### Files Scope

body:
## What

A repeatable end-to-end test for the shop integrations (`SEOProStats_Purchases`): `scripts/shop-test.sh` starts a disposable WordPress in Docker with WooCommerce, Easy Digital Downloads and FluentCart, installs this branch's GitHub zip, makes a visit, places and pays orders through each shop's own code, posts ThriveCart webhooks, processes the buffer and checks the results. It fails on any wrong count, amount, currency or join, or on any PHP message from the plugin. Today this check was a throwaway script made by hand for PR #31; shops change their hooks between versions, so it should run again before each release and whenever the purchases code changes.

## How

Base it on `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (same Docker layout: MariaDB, `wordpress:php<ver>-apache`, `wordpress:cli-php<ver>`, `127.0.0.1` random port, cleanup trap, `--php`, `--wp`, `--ref`, `--zip`, `--keep-log`; source `scripts/lib/plugin.sh`). The working script from PR #31, to turn into the repository's style (Bash 3.2, `local var="$1"`, explicit `return`, ShellCheck clean):

1. Site and plugins: copy a test must-use plugin first, so it sees every request; `wp plugin install <zip> --activate`; `wp plugin install woocommerce easy-digital-downloads fluent-cart --activate` (versions printed; `--shop-versions` may pin them). EDD 3 makes its tables only on its admin path: run `edd_install_component_database_tables(); edd_run_install();` by `wp eval` after activation.
2. Must-use plugin (`scripts/shop-test-mu.php`, copied into the site only): `?spst_test=edd` builds an EDD order with `edd_build_order()` in the visitor's own request (then `edd_pay` completes it from a request with another user agent); `?spst_test=fluentcart` creates a `FluentCart\App\Models\Order` (`total_amount` in cents, `type` `payment`), dispatches `OrderCreated`, then `OrderPaid` twice. It also hooks `doing_it_wrong_run` and logs a backtrace for `_load_textdomain_just_in_time`.
3. Visit: two pageviews by `POST /wp-json/seoprostats/v1/collect` with one browser user agent (a campaign `utm_*` entry and a second page with a fixed page-load ID), then `wp seoprostats process`.
4. WooCommerce block checkout by the Store API with the same user agent and a cookie jar (`GET /wc/store/v1/cart` for the `Nonce` header, `cart/add-item`, `checkout` with `payment_method` `cod` and `bacs`); `bacs` is then completed and set back to processing by `wp wc shop_order update`; one order made by `wp wc shop_order create` must not count.
5. ThriveCart: set `purchases_thrivecart`; HEAD and the `?rest_route=` address answer 200; wrong secret 403; `order.success` recorded; the same `order_id` `duplicate`; `mode=test` `test`; an unknown page-load ID `not-joined`; `order.refund` `ignored`.
6. Process, then assert (by `wp eval` on the events and sessions tables, or `wp seoprostats properties source --event=Purchase --format=json`): exactly woocommerce 2 (USD 79.96 for 2 × 19.99 twice), edd 1 (EUR 49.00), fluentcart 1 (GBP 25.00), thrivecart 1 (USD 997.00), all on the one visit; `doctor` reports 1 ThriveCart order not joined; `debug.log` has no line from the plugin (WooCommerce's own early-translation notice is allowed and listed).

Mailer failures (`sendmail: can't connect`) are expected noise; silence them with a `pre_wp_mail` filter in the must-use plugin.

title: Change log: posts, links, SEO fields, products, plugins, themes, core and settings on the timeline
body:
## What

Phase 3 starts here (`todo/PLANS.md` → Phase 3, `docs/architecture.md` → Integrations → Changes): a change log that records what changed on the site, when, and on which page, as markers for every chart and as facts that explain why traffic, rankings or sales moved. `GET /markers` answers an empty list today.

Changes recorded, each with the page it affects when there is one:

- **Posts and pages** (any public post type): published, unpublished (to draft, private, pending or trash), scheduled post going live, address changed (slug or parent: old and new path), title changed, content changed (words added and removed, word count before and after), internal links added, removed or changed (anchor or target), external links gained and lost (by host), SEO title, meta description and robots (noindex, nofollow, canonical) of Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress and The SEO Framework.
- **Products** (WooCommerce; EDD and FluentCart prices where their hooks allow): out of stock, back in stock, price increased or decreased (regular and sale, in the shop's currency), sale started and ended, coupons published, changed and removed (as promotions).
- **Site**: plugins installed, updated, activated, deactivated and deleted (name and versions); theme switched and updated; WordPress core updated; search engine visibility (`blog_public`), permalink structure, site address and front page settings changed.

## How

- **Table `changes`** (schema v6, `SEOProStats_Schema`): `id`, `ts`, `kind` (small int: a code from a `SEOProStats_Changes::KINDS` map, documented), `path_id` (dict, 0 for site-wide), `object_type` (post, term, product, plugin, theme, core, option), `object_id`, `old`, `new` (short text, 190 chars), `meta` (JSON: words added/removed, link host lists, versions, prices with currency), `source` (1 WordPress, 2 WP-CLI, 3 REST/API, 4 cron, 5 feed, 6 annotation), `user_id`. Keys: `ts`, `(path_id, ts)`, `(kind, ts)`. Kept forever (small; the long-term record). Demo data gets its own table and plausible changes (posts published, a plugin update, a price drop, a product out of stock) so the markers show on demo charts.
- **Recording** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-changes.php`): WordPress hooks only, never on a visitor's page view (writes happen inside requests that already save posts, products, orders or options). `post_updated` (before and after objects) for status, slug, parent, title and content: links from `post_content` with `WP_HTML_Tag_Processor` (`a[href]`; internal = the site's hosts, as the collector's config), words from `wp_strip_all_tags()`, compared before and after; `transition_post_status` for publish and unpublish; `updated_post_meta`/`added_post_meta`/`deleted_post_meta` for the SEO plugins' keys (Yoast `_yoast_wpseo_title`, `_yoast_wpseo_metadesc`, `_yoast_wpseo_meta-robots-noindex`, `_yoast_wpseo_canonical`; Rank Math `rank_math_title`, `rank_math_description`, `rank_math_robots`, `rank_math_canonical_url`; SEOPress `_seopress_titles_title`, `_seopress_titles_desc`, `_seopress_robots_index`, `_seopress_robots_canonical`; The SEO Framework `_genesis_title`, `_genesis_description`, `_genesis_noindex`, `_genesis_canonical_uri`). WooCommerce: `woocommerce_before_product_object_save` (old values from `get_data()`, new from `get_changes()`: `regular_price`, `sale_price`, `stock_status`, `date_on_sale_from/to`), variations likewise; coupons through post status. `upgrader_process_complete`, `activated_plugin`, `deactivated_plugin`, `deleted_plugin`, `switch_theme`, `_core_updated_successfully`, `update_option_{blog_public|permalink_structure|home|siteurl|show_on_front|page_on_front}`. Autosaves, revisions, non-public post types and imports in bulk (`WP_IMPORTING`) are skipped. A post's several changes in one save are separate rows with one `ts`.
- **Reading**: `GET /markers` returns the changes in the range (with `kind`, page path, title, summary text made at read time, `source`, user display name for those who can list users), optional `page` filter, `kinds` filter; `GET /changes` lists them with paging. `wp seoprostats changes [--page=<path>] [--kind=<kind>]`. OpenAPI and `@seoprostats/core` types follow.
- **Privacy**: changes are site facts, not visitor data; no visitor information is involved.

Later issues (not here): markers lane on charts, Changes section and annotations; search engine update markers; snapshots with word diffs and page detail; movers and anomalies.

## Files

### Files Scope

- NEW: `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-changes.php`
- EDIT: `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php` (v6: `changes`)
- EDIT: `includes/class-seoprostats-setup.php`
- EDIT: `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-api.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-cli.php`
- EDIT: `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-demo.php`
- EDIT: `docs/api/openapi.yaml`, `packages/core/src/types.ts`
- EDIT: `docs/architecture.md`, `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, `todo/PLANS.md`, `uninstall.php`

## Check

- `composer install && scripts/lint.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4` pass; visitor pages run no new query (smoke test list), the changes queries use their keys (EXPLAIN in the smoke test).
- Disposable site: publish a post, change its slug, title and content (add an internal and an external link, remove one), set a Yoast description, unpublish it; activate and deactivate a plugin; switch theme; change `blog_public`; with WooCommerce, change a price up and down, mark a product out of stock and back, put it on sale. `wp seoprostats changes --format=json` lists each once with the right page, old and new values; `GET /markers?range=today` returns them.

title: Outside data sources: Search Console, Bing Webmaster, Ahrefs, Semrush, Search Atlas, DataForSEO, Serper, SerpApi
body:
## What

Phase 4 (`todo/PLANS.md` → Phase 4: search): supplement the site's own statistics with outside data sources the owner connects, all opt-in and only adding facts (`docs/architecture.md` → Principles 3):

- **Search Console** (Google) and **Bing Webmaster Tools**: clicks, impressions, position and CTR by page, query, country and device, daily, with backfill (Search Console 16 months).
- **SEO data providers**, with the owner's own API key: Ahrefs, Semrush, Search Atlas, DataForSEO (backlinks, referring domains, organic keywords and positions, domain metrics), and SERP APIs Serper and SerpApi (tracked keywords' positions and SERP features on a schedule).

This is a parent issue: each source becomes its own child issue and pull request, in this order: Search Console, Bing Webmaster, DataForSEO, then the others. It is not dispatched as one piece.

## How (shared shape)

- **Connections** (Settings → Connections): per source, credentials stored encrypted at rest with the site's keys (never in the REST answers or exports), a test button, a schedule, and a monthly request budget so paid APIs never surprise the owner. `wp seoprostats connect <source>` for agents.
- **Storage**: Search Console and Bing into `gsc_*`-shaped tables with an `engine` column (pages, queries, pairs, totals: `clicks`, `impressions`, `pos_impr`), backlinks into `links` (source host and URL, target page, anchor, rel, first and last seen, lost, authority, provider), tracked keywords into a `serp` table (keyword, engine, location, device, day, position, URL, features). Each import run in `imports` so it can be undone.
- **Timeline**: backlinks gained and lost, and ranking moves above a threshold, become `changes` rows (markers), so they line up with traffic.
- **Reports**: Search section (Rankings, Opportunities, Backlinks) per `docs/architecture.md` → Dashboard app, with the provider named on each figure.
- **Cost and privacy**: requests only from cron or the owner's action; nothing on visitor pages; each provider's terms checked before storing its data long term.

## Files

### Files Scope

Each child issue lists its files. Expected: `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-connections.php`, one class per source under `includes/stats/sources/`, schema v7+ tables, `packages/wp-admin/src/Search*.tsx`, `docs/api/openapi.yaml`, `docs/architecture.md`.

## Check

Per child: a disposable site connected with a test key imports a day and a backfill, a second run adds nothing, undo by import id removes it, and the smoke test passes.

title: Search Console: connect with a service-account key, daily import and backfill
body:
## What

First child of #37 (outside data sources), Phase 4 in `todo/PLANS.md`: connect Google Search Console with a service-account key and import its search data daily, with a 16-month backfill, into tables of our own. Also lays the shared ground the later sources use: Settings → Connections, credentials encrypted at rest, an `imports` table so any import can be undone, and the `gsc_*` tables with an `engine` column (Bing Webmaster later writes to the same tables).

Reports on this data (Search section: Rankings, Opportunities) are the next child; this one gets the data in, correct and undoable, and shows its status.

## How

- **Schema v7** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php`): `gsc_pages` (day, engine, path_id), `gsc_queries` (day, engine, query_id), `gsc_pairs` (day, engine, path_id, query_id), `gsc_totals` (day, engine, device, country), each with `clicks`, `impressions`, `pos_impr` (position × impressions, for weighted averages) and `import_id`; `imports` (id, source, status, started, finished, day_from, day_to, rows, meta). Queries are dict text (new kind); pages are path dict ids, the same as visits, so search and visits join by page. Keys for reads by day range and by page/query over a range.
- **Connections** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-connections.php`, new): one option (autoload off) with each source's encrypted credentials, choices (property) and state (last import, backfill progress, last error). Credentials are encrypted with libsodium (`sodium_crypto_secretbox`, bundled with WordPress) using a key derived from the site's salts; never in REST answers, exports or logs. Disconnect deletes them (and, when asked, the source's data).
- **Search Console** (`includes/stats/sources/class-seoprostats-source-search-console.php`, new): service-account JSON key → RS256 JWT (`openssl_sign`) → access token from Google's fixed token address (the key's `token_uri` is not trusted) with the `webmasters.readonly` scope; list the properties the account can read and pick the one for the home URL (domain or URL-prefix), or the one chosen; Search Analytics queries per day for pages, queries, pairs (paged, capped per day) and device × country totals. Addresses become paths only when they belong to the site.
- **Jobs**: the daily cron imports every final day not yet imported (three days back and older); backfill on connect runs in short cron runs a minute apart, newest first, until 16 months are in. All remote requests from cron, WP-CLI or the owner's action only; nothing on visitor pages.
- **Undo and retention**: each run is an `imports` row; undo by id deletes its rows. Pages, queries and pairs are kept 25 months; totals forever (`docs/architecture.md` → Retention).
- **Interfaces**: Settings → Connections tab (paste the key, the service account's address to add in Search Console, property, status, import now, disconnect); REST `GET /connections`, `POST /connections/search-console`, `DELETE /connections/search-console` (administrators); WP-CLI `wp seoprostats connect search-console`, `disconnect`, `search-console import|status|undo`; `wp seoprostats doctor` line.

title: Search section: Rankings from Search Console (report, REST, WP-CLI, demo data)
body:
## What

Second child of #37 (Phase 4 in `todo/PLANS.md`), named as the next step in #43: show the Search Console data that #43 imports. Adds a **Search** section to the dashboard (Rankings): clicks, impressions, CTR and average position for the period, with the comparison, a daily chart, and tables of queries, pages, countries and devices. Choosing a page lists its queries; choosing a query lists its pages. The same report is available as REST `GET /search`, `wp seoprostats search` and the `seoprostats/search` ability. Demo data gets made-up search rows, so the section can be tried without a connection.

## Why

#43 imports search data, but nothing shows it yet. This report is the first place where search figures and the site's own visits appear on the same screen, which is what `docs/architecture.md` → "What it is for" promises. Opportunities (striking distance, CTR gaps, decay) and Bing come in later children.

## How

- **Report** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search.php`, new, `SEOProStats_Search::report($req, $kind, $page, $query)`), following `SEOProStats_Clicks` (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-clicks.php`):
  - The range resolves with `SEOProStats_Query::range()` into site-local days. The period is cut at the newest day with search data (about three days ago), and the comparison (`compare_range()`) gets the same number of days, so missing recent days never look like a drop. The answer gives `through` (newest day) and `first` (oldest day).
  - Totals: clicks, impressions, CTR (clicks ÷ impressions) and the impression-weighted position (`SUM(pos_impr) / SUM(impressions) / 100`), from `gsc_totals` for the site, `gsc_pages` (`path_day`) for one page or pattern, and `gsc_queries` (`query_day`) for one query. Daily (or monthly, past 120 days) points come from the same table.
  - Rows: `queries` (`gsc_queries`, or `gsc_pairs` by `path_day` for one page), `pages` (`gsc_pages`, or `gsc_pairs` by `query_day` for one query), `countries` and `devices` (`gsc_totals`, site only). Ordered by clicks, then impressions; limit and offset. Each row has clicks, impressions, CTR and position, plus the change from the comparison for the rows shown.
  - Only `engine = 1` (Google) for now; the `engine` column is already there for Bing. Every read uses a primary key or `path_day`/`query_day` range; nothing reads visit tables.
  - Cached with `SEOProStats_Query::cached()`. The key includes the newest import, so an import or undo shows at once.
  - Filters from the shared bar: a page filter (`page is` / `matches`) narrows the report like the page box. Visit filters (source, country…) do not apply to search data. The answer lists the filters it ignored, and the screen says so.
  - Connection state for the empty screen: `connected`, plus `has_data`. Demo data is always connected.
- **Interfaces**: REST `GET /search` (`view_seoprostats`, report arguments, plus `kind`, `page`, `query`) in `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-api.php`; `wp seoprostats search [<kind>] [--page=] [--query=]` in `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-cli.php`; ability `seoprostats/search` in `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-abilities.php`.
- **Demo data** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-demo.php`): per final day, search rows for the demo pages and made-up queries (pages, queries, pairs, device × country totals) on the demo tables, written in budgeted steps like the visits. Demo data made before this gets them once.
- **Screen**: `packages/wp-admin/src/Search.tsx` (new): tiles switch the chart metric. Tables switch with buttons (Queries, Pages, Countries, Devices), and a page or query can be chosen and cleared. Page rows get View and Edit links where the person may edit, as in Clicks (`edit_url` added outside the cache). A not-connected state links to Settings → Connections, and an empty state names the newest day. A small chart component uses `@seoprostats/charts` `createTimeseries` with a table for screen readers. Types go in `packages/core/src/types.ts`, the `search` view in `packages/core/src/state.ts`, the tab in `App.tsx`, the hook in `api.ts`, and the submenu in `includes/admin/class-seoprostats-dashboard.php`.
- **Docs**: `docs/api/openapi.yaml` (`/search` and its schemas), `docs/architecture.md` (Reports, Interfaces, Dashboard app, Demo data), README.md, readme.txt, changelog.txt, `todo/PLANS.md`.

## Files

### Files Scope

- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search.php` (new)
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-api.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-cli.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-abilities.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-demo.php`

## Check

title: Search Console: one-click Sign in with Google through a hosted relay (Cloudflare Worker); needs owner setup
body:
## What

One-click **Sign in with Google** for the Search Console connection: the owner chooses the button on Settings → Connections, approves read access on Google's own consent screen, picks a property, and is connected. No Google Cloud project, service account or key file on their side. The service-account key (today's method) stays as the choice that involves no server of ours.

**Held for the owner's setup** (`no-auto-dispatch`, `needs-credentials`): it needs a Google OAuth app and a small relay that the plugin's owner runs. Code can start once the setup below is done.

## Why

The service-account setup is six steps in Google Cloud and Search Console (now linked step by step on the Connections tab). Most site owners expect a Google sign-in screen, as other SEO plugins offer. A Google OAuth app has a fixed list of redirect addresses and a client secret, so a plugin installed on many sites cannot use one directly: the sign-in has to go through one fixed address that we run, and so does every token refresh (refreshing needs the secret, which must never ship in the plugin). An owner-made OAuth client was considered and dropped: it is as much Google Cloud work as the service account, with an "unverified app" warning on top.

## How

### Owner setup (blocks the code)

1. **Domain**: a domain (or subdomain) we own, its DNS on Cloudflare (free plan), with a homepage and a privacy policy for the sign-in service. Google needs these for the consent screen and verification, and they must be on a domain we can verify; a `workers.dev` address cannot be used.
2. **Cloudflare**: a Worker on that domain (Workers free plan; check the current daily request and CPU limits, which an hourly refresh per connected site has to fit), with the client ID and secret stored as Worker secrets, never in the repository.
3. **Google Cloud**: a project owned by us; Search Console API turned on; OAuth consent screen (External, In production) with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/webmasters.readonly`; a Web application OAuth client whose only redirect URI is the Worker's callback address.
4. **Google verification**: the Search Console scope is expected to be a sensitive scope (confirm in the console), so Google reviews the app (homepage, privacy policy, domain verification, a demo video of the sign-in). Until it passes, users see an "unverified app" screen and the app is capped at a small number of users, which is fine for testing.

### Relay (Cloudflare Worker), stateless

- `GET /start`: the plugin sends the site's return address (its wp-admin Connections URL) and a one-time nonce it keeps for the signed-in admin. The Worker signs both into OAuth `state` (HMAC with a Worker secret), then redirects to Google's consent screen with `access_type=offline` and `prompt=consent`.
- `GET /callback`: the Worker checks `state`, exchanges the code for tokens at Google's token endpoint (`https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token`, as the plugin already uses), and hands the tokens to the site in an auto-submitting HTML form POST to the return address (never in a URL, so they never land in logs or browser history). The plugin checks the nonce, stores the refresh token encrypted like today's key, and lists the properties.
- `POST /refresh`: the plugin sends its refresh token; the Worker adds the client secret, asks Google for an access token and returns it. Google rejects invalid tokens, so the Worker needs no list of sites.
- Nothing is stored and no tokens are logged (Worker logs off or redacted). Disconnecting revokes the token with Google directly from the plugin (revocation needs no secret).
- Where the Worker code lives is the owner's choice: a folder in this repository left out of plugin zips by `.distignore`, or a repository of its own.

### Plugin

- `includes/stats/sources/class-seoprostats-source-search-console.php`: a second credential type (refresh token) beside the service-account key; access tokens from `/refresh` instead of a signed JWT; the import job does not change.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-connections.php`: store the refresh token encrypted (same secretbox and key as today), never returned.
- `includes/admin/class-seoprostats-connections-tab.php` and `admin/js/seoprostats-connections.js`: a **Sign in with Google** button first, the key steps under it as the other way; the return handler with nonce check and property choice.
- `readme.txt` → External services: the relay (what is sent: the site's return address and its tokens; when: connecting and each refresh; its terms and privacy policy), and the same in `README.md` and `docs/architecture.md` (Search Console).

## Acceptance

- On a test site: sign in with Google, pick a property, the history import starts; an hour later the access token is refreshed through the relay and imports continue; disconnect revokes the token with Google.
- No token or secret appears in a URL, a log line of the Worker or the site, or any REST, WP-CLI or screen output.
- The service-account method still works unchanged.
- `scripts/lint.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` pass.

## Files

### Files Scope

- `includes/stats/sources/class-seoprostats-source-search-console.php`
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-connections.php`
- `includes/admin/class-seoprostats-connections-tab.php`
- `admin/js/seoprostats-connections.js`
- `readme.txt`, `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `todo/PLANS.md`
- Relay code: path not known until the owner chooses (see How → Relay).

title: Search Opportunities: striking distance, low CTR and losing clicks with likely causes
body:
## What

Search → **Opportunities**: what to work on next, from the imported Search Console days (Phase 4 in `todo/PLANS.md`; For #37).

- **Striking distance**: a page's query at average position 4–20 with enough impressions, where moving up to the top three would bring most clicks. Potential clicks = impressions × (the site's own CTR at position 3 − the pair's CTR).
- **Low CTR**: a page's query in the top 10 whose CTR is well under the site's own CTR at that position (title and snippet work). Missed clicks = impressions × expected CTR − clicks.
- **Losing clicks** (decay): pages with fewer clicks than the previous period of the same length, each with a likely cause: **position** (it ranks lower), **demand** (fewer searches, position steady) or **CTR** (as many searches and the same place, fewer clicks), the queries that lost most, and the site's recorded changes on that page in the two periods (the change log, Phase 3), so cause and effect sit together.

Expected CTR comes from the site's own data in the period (clicks ÷ impressions by rounded position, 1–20, made never to rise with position), not from published curves; with too little data a cautious default curve is used and the answer says so.

REST `GET /opportunities` (`kind=striking|ctr|decay`), `wp seoprostats opportunities [<kind>]`, the ability `seoprostats/opportunities`, OpenAPI, and a Search sub-tab beside Rankings. Choosing a row opens it in Rankings (page and query chosen).

Content performance (search joined with the site's visits and conversions per page) is left for its own child: it reads the visit tables and needs its own cost check.

## Why

Rankings shows what happened; Opportunities says where effort pays. Losing clicks with its likely cause and the changes made to the page is the "cause and effect" the plugin is for (`docs/architecture.md` → What it is for).

## How

- New `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-opportunities.php`, reusing `SEOProStats_Search`'s days, bounds, scope and metrics (make the needed helpers non-private, unchanged). Reads `gsc_pairs` and `gsc_pages` by their primary key (engine, day); the period is cut at the newest final day and to its newest 91 days, so a year never reads every pair; the answer gives the range used. Cached with `SEOProStats_Query::cached()` and the imports version, as `search` is.
- Thresholds as constants, scaled by days in the period (minimum impressions; decay: at least 20% and a minimum of clicks lost).
- Changes per page: `SEOProStats_Changes` rows by `path_id` over both periods (check its existing reader and key first).
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-api.php`, `class-seoprostats-cli.php`, `class-seoprostats-abilities.php`: as `search` is wired; `docs/api/openapi.yaml`.
- `packages/wp-admin/src/`: Search gets Rankings | Opportunities; three cards with tables; WordPress components.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-demo.php`: a few demo queries that lose position, demand or CTR in the last weeks, one in striking distance with a low CTR, and a demo change on the page that drops, so each card shows something (demo days are regenerated on the next demo catch-up).
- Docs: `docs/architecture.md` (Search → Opportunities, routes, CLI, abilities), `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, `todo/PLANS.md`.

## Check

- Demo data: each card lists rows; decay rows name a cause and the demo change; choosing a row opens Rankings with it.
- Live site without Search Console: links to Settings → Connections as Rankings does.
- EXPLAIN of each query uses the primary key with a day range; a year period reads at most 91 days.
- `scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/smoke-test.sh`; OpenAPI parses.

## Files

### Files Scope

- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-opportunities.php` (new)
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search.php`
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-api.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-cli.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-abilities.php`

title: feat: keep the Changes section's page and group in the view address
body:
## What

Follow-up to #24 (PR #54): the Changes section's choices still live in React state and are lost on reload, unlike every other section's. These are the page box ("Only on page", applied value only) and the group menu ("Show": All changes or one group) in `packages/wp-admin/src/Changes.tsx:84-100`.

## Decision needed in the implementation (self-contained)

Changes starts its page box from the page filter (`filteredPage(state.filters)`, `Changes.tsx:86`). If the address holds `page`, decide which wins when both exist. Recommended: the address `page` wins when present; with no `page` in the address, fall back to the page filter as today. "Any page" then has to clear the filter's influence too. One way is a sentinel-free rule: "Any page" writes no `page` and the box shows empty only when no page filter is set. Pick the simplest rule that keeps old addresses unchanged and write it in `docs/architecture.md`.

## How

- `packages/core/src/state.ts`: add `group?: ChangeGroup` (validated with `oneOf(CHANGE_GROUPS, …)`) and reuse `page` for `view === 'changes'` in `sectionParams()`. Add `group` to `SECTION_VALUES` so `switchView()` drops it.
- `packages/wp-admin/src/Changes.tsx`: read `state.page` / `state.group` and write with `update({ page })` / `update({ group })`. Keep the typed box as a draft that follows the address (the same `useEffect` as `Clicks.tsx`). The offset reset (`Changes.tsx:100`) keeps working on `[page, group]`.
- `docs/architecture.md` → Dashboard: add a Changes row to the address table. `changelog.txt`: extend the Unreleased "address keeps each section's choices" line.
- Reference pattern: Clicks `kind`/`page` in PR #54.

title: Content performance: search joined with each page's search visits and goal conversions (Search → Content)
body:
## What

Content performance, the next Phase 4 item in `todo/PLANS.md`: one table per page that joins what Google showed (Search Console clicks, impressions, CTR, position) with what the visits from search did on the site (search visits landing on the page, bounce rate, views per visit, time) and how many of them reached a goal (conversions, conversion rate). It answers "which content earns its search traffic, and which only ranks".

It is a third tab under Search: **Rankings · Opportunities · Content**.

## Design and cost check

The plan says this reads the visit tables and needs its own cost check. Reading `sessions` for every report (a year of visits, filtered by channel and grouped by entry page) would not use a covering index and grows with traffic, so:

- **A daily summary of search landings.** The rollup (`SEOProStats_Rollup::summarise()`) writes one more `daily` dimension, `SEARCH_LANDING = 18`: visits whose channel is organic search, by entry page (`val` = entry `path_id`), with the usual visit sums. One extra `INSERT … SELECT` per day, on the day's sessions by `started`, like the other session dimensions. It is not a `SEOProStats_Query::DIMENSIONS` entry, so the report engine never treats it as a filter or breakdown.
- **Refill backwards.** Days summarised before this change have no rows of the new dimension. The minute job refills them newest first, one day per query (delete and insert that day's rows of dimension 18 only), within the rollup's budget, and only as far back as search data exists (Search Console keeps 16 months; the floor is the oldest of: first `gsc_totals` day, first visit, oldest kept visit). Progress is `landings` in the rollup state option. Demo data refills the same way when it is topped up. Until it is done the answer names the first complete day (`filled_from`) and the screen says so.
- **The report reads only indexes.** Search figures from `gsc_pages` (primary key, or `path_day` with page filters) as Search does; search visits from `daily` by `dim_val_day`; conversions for **one chosen goal** (default: the first) with the Goals report's own query (`events` by `name_ts` or `pageviews` by `path_ts`, joined to sessions by the primary key), grouped by the visit's entry page and limited to organic search visits. So the cost is the goal's hits in the period, as for the Goals report, and never the whole visit table.
- Days are the search days (`SEOProStats_Search::days()`, cut at the newest imported day) so a page never seems to lose visits for days Search Console has not reported yet. Page filters apply; other filters are named in `ignored`, as on Search.

Rows are every page with search clicks or search visits in the period, merged by `path_id`, sorted by clicks (`sort=visits` and `sort=conversions` also offered), paged, with the comparison's figures and changes for the rows shown, and editor links added after the shared cache (as Search's pages).

## Files

- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-rollup.php` — `SEARCH_LANDING`, its insert in `summarise()`, `refill()` called from `run()`.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-content.php` (new) — the report.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-conversions.php` — a public per-entry-page count of one goal's visits.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-api.php` (`GET /content`), `class-seoprostats-cli.php` (`wp seoprostats content`), `class-seoprostats-abilities.php` (`seoprostats/content`), `class-seoprostats-demo.php` (refill on top-up), `docs/api/openapi.yaml`.
- `packages/core/src/types.ts`, `state.ts`; `packages/wp-admin/src/api.ts`, `Search.tsx` (tab), `Content.tsx` (new), `dashboard.css`.
- Docs: `docs/architecture.md` (Storage `daily`, Processing, Reports), `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, `todo/PLANS.md`.

Reference pattern: `SEOProStats_Opportunities` (#53, PR #56) for the report, its interfaces and its tab.

## Verification

- `composer install && scripts/lint.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` in the worktree (repository rule while Actions are off).
- Demo data: the Content tab lists pages with clicks, search visits and goal conversions; the refill runs and `filled_from` clears; `EXPLAIN` of each query names its key.
- Browser check of the tab (desktop and 390px), keyboard tab switching, no console or API errors.
