title: SEO decision loop: turn the gathered data into audits, ranked plans and measured cause and effect
body:
Planning-only: decide, design and split into worker-ready child issues. Do not build the features in this issue.

## Goal

SEO Pro Stats already gathers most of what an SEO audit needs: visits and conversions, the site's changes, search engine updates and Search Console data, all on one timeline. What it lacks is the step from data to decisions. The plugin should help an owner, or an AI agent through REST, WP-CLI and abilities, to:

1. **find** what is wrong or could be better (an audit);
2. **decide** what to do first (a ranked plan with reasons);
3. **record** what was changed and what it was expected to do;
4. **measure** whether it worked, against pages that were left alone and with the confounders named;
5. **feed back** what was learned into the next round.

This issue reviews what aidevops knows about SEO and what the plugin's data can support. Its output is a design and a set of child issues in build order.

## Why

Ranking work is usually done from one-off audits and memory. Once a page is changed, nobody checks a few weeks later whether clicks, position or conversions moved, or whether a search update or another change explains the result. The plugin already holds the changes, the markers and the search and visit data, so it can close that loop on the site itself, privately and cheaply.

## What exists (verify against `HEAD` before relying on it)

| Area | Where | Gives |
|---|---|---|
| Search Console import | `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search-import.php`, `includes/stats/sources/class-seoprostats-source-search-console.php` | Daily clicks, impressions and position by page, query, page × query, device × country; 16 months back (`gsc_*`, engine 1) |
| Rankings | `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search.php` | Search report with comparison and page ↔ query drill-down |
| Opportunities | `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-opportunities.php` | Striking distance, low CTR against the site's own CTR curve, pages losing clicks with a likely cause and that page's changes |
| Content | `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-content.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-conversions.php` | Clicks joined with visits from search and one goal's conversions per page |
| Changes and markers | `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-changes.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search-updates.php` | Post edits (status, address, title, words, links), SEO plugin fields, product, plugin, theme and core changes, notes; Google updates as spans |
| Goals and revenue | `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-goals.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-purchases.php` | What a visit is worth |
| Interfaces | `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-api.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-cli.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-abilities.php`, `docs/api/openapi.yaml` | REST, WP-CLI, abilities for MCP clients |
| Plan | `todo/PLANS.md` | Planned: page snapshots and word diffs, movers and anomalies with causes, Bing, backlinks, referral spikes, vitals, crawlers and AI bots, alerts, shared reports, "aidevops SEO loop recipes" |

Design rules: `docs/architecture.md` and `AGENTS.md` (private by design; visitor pages pay nothing; every report query uses an index; portable `packages/`; write as if public).

## What aidevops documents (inputs to the review)

Paths are in the aidevops repository (`.agents/seo/`). Read them; take the methods, not the wording.

| Method | aidevops file | Data the plugin has or could get |
|---|---|---|
| Audit order: crawl and index → technical → on-page → content quality → authority; findings as issue, impact, evidence, fix, priority | `seo-audit-skill.md` | On-page facts from WordPress itself (titles, descriptions, headings, images, links, noindex and canonical from SEO plugins); index facts need Search Console or Bing URL inspection |
| Opportunity types: quick wins, striking distance, low CTR, cannibalisation (several URLs for one query is evidence, not proof) | `ranking-opportunities.md` | `gsc_pairs`; cannibalisation is not built yet |
| Pre-registered experiments: hypothesis, scope, baseline, comparison group, exact intervention and time, sampling and review window, confounders; result retain, revise, stop or inconclusive; keep null and negative results | `seo-geo-experiment-design.md` | `changes` gives the intervention and time; search and visit data give the outcome; search updates and other changes are the confounders |
| Scorecard per cycle: baseline, current, delta, target, evidence; unknown is not zero; counts beside rates | `ai-search-kpi-template.md` | Any report can give baseline and current for a set of pages |
| Entity register, evidence independence, internal-link graph (orphans, contextual inbound links, anchors, links through redirects) | `entity-evidence-audit.md` | Links can be read from post content on save and in cron, without crawling |
| Content disposition: keep, update, merge, remove or abstain, review-only, protecting pages that earn revenue | `content-disposition.md` | Search, visits and conversions per page (Content report) |
| Search targets registry, priority score (45% business value, 35% opportunity, 20% position), tracking runs, movers | `keywords-standard.md` | The plugin could read a site's chosen targets and report on them; `keywords track --source export` takes export files (`data-export.md`) |
| E-E-A-T criteria (authorship, citation, effort, originality, intent, quality, writing) | `eeat-score.md` | Author pages, references and dates from WordPress; the scoring itself is judgment, so an agent's job, not the plugin's |
| Cross-engine index checks | `bing-webmaster-tools.md`, `google-search-console.md` | Bing import (next plan item) and URL inspection |

## Candidate features to assess, rank and split

A first ranking; the review should confirm, merge or drop each with reasons.

1. **Experiments (change → outcome).** The owner, or an agent, records a hypothesis on a page or group of pages: the change, the primary measure (clicks, position, CTR, visits from search, conversions), the expected direction and threshold, and the review date. A change log entry can start one. At review the plugin compares the same number of days before and after (same weekdays), against comparable pages that did not change in the window, and lists search updates and other site changes in the window as confounders. Result: retain, revise, stop or inconclusive, with the numbers. Experiments appear on the timeline. Builds on `changes`, annotations and the Search reports.
2. **Decision queue.** One ranked list of things to do, from Opportunities, losing clicks, Content and the audits below. Each item says why it is there and how its score is made, for example potential clicks × value of a visit from search (goal conversions and revenue) × confidence ÷ effort. Items move through proposed, accepted, done and measured; a done item opens an experiment.
3. **Page detail with snapshots** (already in Phase 3). Everything about one page together: search, visits, conversions, changes, word diffs, experiments and queue items.
4. **Cannibalisation candidates.** Queries where two or more pages get impressions, and where the page Google shows switches between weeks, with each page's clicks and position. Shown as a candidate to review, never as a fault.
5. **On-site content audit from WordPress.** Facts read from posts and SEO plugin fields on save and in cron batches, never on visitor pages: title and description length and duplicates, H1 count, word count, images without alt text, last updated date, noindex and canonical, thin pages with impressions but no clicks. Each finding ties to the page's search and conversion figures, so the ones that matter come first.
6. **Internal link graph.** Contextual links between posts (read from content), orphan pages, pages that earn conversions with few links in, and pages that rank for a query but do not link to the page meant for it.
7. **Indexation.** Published pages with no impressions after N days; sitemap URLs against pages with impressions; Search Console and Bing URL inspection for chosen pages within their quotas.
8. **Refresh planner.** Losing clicks plus content age, last update and conversions to protect: update, merge or leave, as a proposal.
9. **Search targets.** Import the site's chosen queries and their intended pages (the aidevops `context/keywords/` format, or a simple list); report their positions and flag when another page ranks for one.
10. **Movers and anomalies with possible causes** (already planned), feeding the queue.
11. **AI answers.** Crawler and AI bot visits and AI referrals (Phase 5), and imported AI-answer captures, kept separate from search ranking.
12. **Agent interface.** REST, WP-CLI and abilities for the queue and experiments; an export that aidevops can import (check `data-export.md` and `keywords-standard.md` for the format); the "aidevops SEO loop recipes" in `docs/`.
13. **Digest.** The weekly email (Phase 6) carries the top queue items and experiments due for review.

## Constraints

- Private by design and no cost on visitor pages; every new read uses an index (check with `EXPLAIN` in the smoke test). New stored facts get retention settings.
- Say "associated with", not "caused", unless a comparison group supports it; show denominators, coverage (the Search Console import keeps the top pages and queries per day) and missing data. An inconclusive result stays inconclusive.
- WordPress components and patterns in wp-admin (`DESIGN.md`); the API contract and `packages/core` stay free of WordPress and React.
- Write as if public: describe features in our own words, and name no other analytics products as sources.

## Deliverables

1. A design section, either `docs/seo-loop.md` or a section of `docs/architecture.md`: the loop, each chosen feature's data, storage, cost, interfaces and place in the app, and what was dropped and why.
2. `todo/PLANS.md` updated with the chosen items in build order and their dependencies.
3. One worker-ready child issue per feature: Files Scope, reference pattern (the nearest existing report class), verification (`composer install && scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/smoke-test.sh`, a check on the preview site) and acceptance criteria. Link them from this issue; give this issue `parent-task` if it stays open as their parent.
4. A short list of changes aidevops itself would need (for example a recipe that reads the plugin's REST), for the owner to file there.

### Files Scope

- `docs/seo-loop.md`
- `docs/architecture.md`
- `todo/PLANS.md`

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes in the worktree.
- Every child issue passes `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check <N> "<body>" 1`.
- Each plan item in `todo/PLANS.md` links to its issue.

## Acceptance

- The design names, for each feature kept, the tables and indexes it reads or adds, and shows that no visitor page does more work.
- Experiments and the decision queue are either designed with their data model and review rules, or explicitly dropped with a reason.
- No child issue proposes a feature that needs an outside service unless it is opt-in, as in `docs/architecture.md` → Integrations.
- No other analytics products, private sites or local paths are named in the design, the plan or the issues.

title: Bing Webmaster Tools as a second search engine: import, and Search reports by engine
body:
For #37 (outside data sources), the second source after Search Console. `todo/PLANS.md` → Phase 4: "Bing Webmaster Tools as a second search engine".

## What

Connect Bing Webmaster Tools with the owner's API key (Bing Webmaster Tools → Settings → API access), import what Bing's API gives into the `gsc_*` tables as engine 2 (`SEOProStats_Schema::ENGINE_BING`, already in the schema), and let Search → Rankings, Opportunities and Content show either engine.

## What Bing's API gives (checked against the live API)

| Method | Gives | Grain |
|---|---|---|
| `GetUserSites` | Verified sites | |
| `GetRankAndTrafficStats` | Site clicks and impressions, no position | Daily, about 16 months, ends about three days ago |
| `GetQueryStats` | Top 100 queries per week: clicks, impressions, average impression position (whole places) | Weekly; a week dated D holds D−7 to D−1 |
| `GetPageStats` | Top 100 pages per week, the same figures | Weekly |
| `GetPageQueryStats` (`page`) | One page's queries per week | Weekly, one request per page |

No device or country. Dates come as `/Date(ms)/` at midnight UTC. Page addresses come as Bing knows them (with or without `www.`).

## How

- `includes/stats/sources/class-seoprostats-source-bing.php`: connect (API key, site picked from the verified sites that match the site's address), the requests, and the answers turned into rows.
- `SEOProStats_Connections::SOURCES` gains `bing`.
- `SEOProStats_Search_Import`: a run for sources whose API answers whole periods at once (Bing): daily totals, weekly pages and queries (each week's figures stored on its last day), then each page's queries in later runs within the budget; replaced by day like Search Console's, each run an `imports` row that can be undone.
- Site position for Bing: the week's average over its top queries, weighted by impressions, given to each day of that week (Bing gives none per day); said so in the answer and on screen.
- Reports take `engine` (`google`, `bing`); REST, WP-CLI and abilities pass it; the Search section gets an engine switch when Bing is connected or has data; countries and devices are Google only.
- Settings → Connections: a Bing card with its setup steps.
- Demo data: Bing rows made from the demo's Google rows, by week.

## Check

- `composer install && scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/smoke-test.sh`.
- A test site connected with a real key imports daily totals, weeks and pairs; a second run adds nothing new; undo removes an import's rows.
- Search → Rankings, Opportunities and Content with Bing chosen, live and demo; `EXPLAIN` keeps the existing keys.

title: Query coverage: search queries a page does not cover, questions and focus keywords (with or without an SEO plugin)
body:
## What

Query coverage: which search queries a page shows for that its own words do not cover, and which of them are questions, built on the Search Console days SEO Pro Stats already imports. Works with any SEO plugin or none; when Rank Math, Yoast SEO or SEOPress is active, the page's focus keywords are checked too.

## Why

A page often gets impressions for queries it never mentions. Putting those words (or an answer to the question) in the title, a heading or the text is one of the cheapest search gains, and the data is already in `gsc_pairs`. No extra import, no visitor-page cost.

## How

- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-coverage.php` (new): one page's queries in the period (newest 91 search days, top 200 by impressions, read by `path_day`), each matched against the page's title, SEO title and description, headings and text; question detection; focus keywords from SEO plugin meta (filter `seoprostats_focus_keywords`). Cached like other reports (`SEOProStats_Query::cached`), keyed by the post's modified time.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-opportunities.php`: fourth kind `missing` (pairs in the top 20 with enough impressions whose page lacks the query's words), bounded to the top candidate pages; reuses the coverage matcher.
- REST `GET /coverage` (`page` or `post`), WP-CLI `wp seoprostats coverage`, ability `seoprostats/coverage`, OpenAPI.
- `packages/core`: types and the same matcher in TypeScript, so the editor re-checks as people write.
- Editor: a "Search queries" panel in the block editor's document sidebar and a meta box in the classic editor.
- Dashboard: Search → Opportunities gets a "Missing from the page" card.
- Demo data: page text for the demo pages so the report shows on demo data.

## Verification

- `composer install && scripts/lint.sh`, `npm run check && npm run build`, `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (Docker).
- REST `/coverage?page=/blog/speed-up-wordpress/&data=demo` and `/opportunities?kind=missing&data=demo` answer with rows.

title: Chart y-axis labels round 2.5 steps (0, 3, 5, 8) on small counts
body:
## Origin

Found while verifying PR #65 (Bing Webmaster Tools) on the preview site: Search → Rankings for one page over 90 days with Bing (weekly clicks of 10–12) drew y-axis labels `0, 3, 5, 8, 10, 13`. The chart code is unchanged by that PR, so this predates it and shows on any chart whose top value is small, Google or visits alike.

## What

The main time-series chart's y-axis labels stay exact: whole-number steps for counts (clicks, impressions, visits), and labels that show the real tick value (no `2.5` printed as `3`).

## Why

Labels that are rounded tick values look like wrong data (`3` and `8` sit on gridlines that are really 2.5 and 7.5), which undermines trust in a statistics screen.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Known file and library (uPlot axis `incrs`/`splits`), but the worker chooses between integer-only steps per series and formatting fractional ticks, and checks every caller of the chart.

## How (Approach)

- Cause: `packages/charts/src/timeseries.ts` sets the y axis (second entry of `axes`, around line 145) with no `incrs`, so uPlot uses its default steps, which include 2.5 and 25; `values` then calls `getConfig().formatValue(v)`, which rounds counts to whole numbers.
- Preferred fix: give the y axis whole-number steps when the series are counts, e.g. `incrs: [1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000, 20000, 50000, 100000, 200000, 500000, 1000000]`, behind a config flag (such as `integer: true`) set by callers whose metric is a count; rates (CTR, bounce rate) and averages (position, duration) keep fractional steps. The x axis already uses explicit `incrs` (line 142) as the pattern.
- Check every caller of the time-series chart in `packages/wp-admin/src` (`rg -n "timeseries|TimeSeries" packages/wp-admin/src`) and set the flag where the metric is a count. `packages/charts` must stay free of WordPress and React (AGENTS.md → Portable underneath).
- Rebuild (`npm run build`) and commit `assets/build/` with the source (DEVELOPMENT.md → JavaScript builds).

### Files Scope

- `packages/charts/src/timeseries.ts`
- `packages/wp-admin/src/components/MainChart.tsx`
- `assets/build/dashboard.js`
- `assets/build/dashboard.asset.php`
- `assets/build/share.js`
- `assets/build/share.asset.php`
- `docs/images/gh66-count-chart.png`

Integration evidence: the existing shared-report entry point bundles Overview and MainChart, so the chart fix also changes its generated JavaScript and asset hash. Both builds must be committed for `npm run build` and `scripts/lint.sh build` to remain reproducible. No open PR overlaps these files at scope recovery.

Screenshot evidence: the requested desktop chart screenshot is kept in `docs/images/gh66-count-chart.png` and embedded in the PR, captured on an isolated demo site. No source or build overlap is introduced by this evidence file.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With demo data (`wp seoprostats demo make`), Search → Rankings → Bing → page `/blog/speed-up-wordpress/` over 90 days draws y-axis labels that are whole numbers on whole-number gridlines (for example 0, 2, 4 … or 0, 5, 10 …), never `3` and `8` together.
2. A rate or average chart (CTR or average position) still shows fractional labels where its range is small.
3. `scripts/lint.sh` passes (including `build`, which fails on stale `assets/build/`); put a desktop screenshot of the chart in the PR.

## Context & Decisions

- Checks run locally for now (AGENTS.md): run `composer install && scripts/lint.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` and put the results in the PR.
- Out of scope: x-axis labels, chart colours, the Bing period logic.

title: Search: Combined engine (Google + Bing + any added later)
body:
## Origin

Owner request after Bing Webmaster Tools landed (#62, PR #65): a **Combined** choice beside **Google** and **Bing** that adds up every connected search engine, including any added later.

## What

`engine=all` (shown as **Combined**) for Search → Rankings, Opportunities and Content, in wp-admin, the REST API, WP-CLI (`--engine=all`) and the abilities. It sums every engine that has data, so a site sees its whole search traffic in one place.

## Why

Most sites want "how is search doing" before "how is Google doing". Having to add Google and Bing by hand hides the real total, and each new engine would make that worse.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The product decisions are made below and the storage already supports it (one set of `gsc_*` tables keyed by `engine`), but the change crosses PHP reports, three interfaces, shared state and the React app.

## How (Approach)

Decisions (made here; follow them):

- **Value and label.** `all` in `SEOProStats_Search::ENGINES` handling (not a stored engine code) and in `SEARCH_ENGINES` (`packages/core/src/types.ts`). The engine switch shows **Combined** after the engines, only when `engines` lists two or more. The default stays `google`, so existing addresses and answers don't change.
- **Sums.** `clicks`, `impressions` and `pos_impr` add up across engines. CTR = clicks / impressions, and position = pos_impr / impressions (`metrics()`), which gives an impression-weighted average. Bing's daily totals already carry a position (their week's, see `day_position()` in `includes/stats/sources/class-seoprostats-source-bing.php`). Page paths and query text share dictionary IDs across engines, so rows for the same query or page merge.
- **Period.** It ends at the *earliest* of the engines' newest days (`bounds()` per engine, take the minimum `to`), so one engine's lag never looks like a drop. If any engine is in `WEEKLY`, pass `$weekly = true` to `days()` (whole weeks) and use `grain` `week` for a page or query, anchored on the weekly engine's newest week (`week_end()`).

- **SQL.** `scope()` / `scope_on()` and the Opportunities and Content queries filter `engine = %d`. For `all`, use `engine IN (…)` of the engines with data. The primary keys start `(engine, day, …)`, so each engine is still a range read. Check with `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (EXPLAIN gate) and on demo data.
- **Days.** Engines keep their own days (Google Pacific time, Bing UTC). Combined adds them as they are; say so in the docs.
- **Source line.** For example "Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools, final days through …" (`sourceName()` in `Search.tsx` and its Content counterpart).

body:
## Origin

Owner request: Search should list its figures by day, as a **Days** tab after Queries, Pages, Countries and Devices, as search tools usually do.

## What

A `days` kind in Search → Rankings: one row per point of the chart (day, week or month, as the chart's `grain`), newest first, with clicks, impressions, CTR and average position. It works for the whole site, a page, a query, and every engine.

## Why

The chart shows the shape, but reading exact figures for a given day (the day after a change, an outage, a launch) means hovering point by point. A table also lets agents and CSV-minded users read the series directly.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Decided behaviour that reuses the existing series, but it touches PHP, three interfaces, shared state and the React table.

## How (Approach)

Decisions:

- **Rows are the chart's points.** Build them from `series()` in `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search.php` (same scope, period and `grain`), so the table always agrees with the chart. Sort newest first and page them with the existing `limit` / `offset` / `more`.
- **Label.** The tab reads **Days**. When `grain` is `week` (a Bing page or query) or `month` (over 120 days), the column heading says Week or Month, and the row label is the period (for example "Sep 18 – Sep 24"), using the date helpers in `packages/wp-admin/src/dates.ts`.
- **No per-row comparison column.** Days don't pair one-to-one across periods. The totals above the chart keep the comparison.
- **Every engine.** Bing keeps Days (unlike countries and devices): update `sectionParams()` in `packages/core/src/state.ts`, which limits Bing's tabs to queries and pages, and the `kinds` list in `packages/wp-admin/src/Search.tsx`.
- Add `days` to `KINDS` (PHP) and `SEARCH_KINDS` (`packages/core/src/types.ts`), and to the `kind` enums and descriptions in the REST API, WP-CLI and abilities.

title: Search: Search appearance tab (rich result types, from Search Console)
body:
## Origin

Owner request: a **Search appearance** tab in Search → Rankings, like Search Console's, showing clicks and impressions by result type (video, product snippets, review snippets, forums and so on) where the data exists.

## What

Import Search Console's search appearance figures by day and show them as an **Appearance** tab for the whole site (Google only), with clicks, impressions, CTR and position for each appearance, against the previous period. It's also available in the REST API, WP-CLI and the abilities.

## Why

Rich results change clicks without any change in rank. Seeing that product or review snippets gained or lost impressions explains movements that the queries and pages tabs can't.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** API rules are verified and the storage and import design is decided below. The work is a known pattern (another `gsc_*` table and import kind) across schema, import, reports, interfaces and demo data.

## How (Approach)

Search Console API rules (read 2026-10-07):
- `searchAppearance` can only be grouped **alone**. It can't be combined with date, page, query, country or device. Rows can be **filtered** by `searchAppearance` (`equals`) while grouping by other dimensions. Discover the values with a standalone grouping first.
- Search appearance figures are aggregated by page.
- Current values include `AMP_BLUE_LINK`, `AMP_TOP_STORIES`, `AMP_IMAGE_RESULT`, `VIDEO`, `PRODUCT_SNIPPETS`, `MERCHANT_LISTINGS`, `REVIEW_SNIPPET`, `FORUMS` and `AMP_STORY`. Don't hard-code the list: store whatever is returned.

Sources: https://developers.google.com/webmaster-tools/v1/how-tos/all-your-data and https://developers.google.com/webmaster-tools/v1/searchanalytics/query (verify again before coding).

Decisions:

- **Storage.** New table `gsc_appearance` in `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php`: `engine, day, appearance_id` (dictionary ID, as queries use), `clicks, impressions, pos_impr, import_id`, with `PRIMARY KEY (engine, day, appearance_id)`. Add it to the tables list (so uninstall drops it) and bump the schema version. Retention, undo and reimport follow the other `gsc_*` tables (by `import_id`).
- **Import.** In `includes/stats/sources/class-seoprostats-source-search-console.php` and `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search-import.php`, for each import range:
  1. Make one request grouped by `searchAppearance` alone to find the values in that range.
  2. For each value, make one request grouped by `date` with a `searchAppearance equals <value>` filter.
  3. Store the rows.

  Keep within the existing request budget and lock, and carry on next run if the budget runs out (as page-query pairs do for Bing).
- **Report.** An `appearance` kind for the whole site only (like countries and devices; empty with a page or query). It reads `gsc_appearance` for the period and the comparison. Under the table, note that one search can show several appearances, so these don't add up to the site's totals.
- **Labels.** Readable names for the known values in the admin app (for example `PRODUCT_SNIPPETS` → "Product snippets"). An unknown value gets its raw name in sentence case.
- **Bing.** It has no equivalent breakdown, so the tab is hidden for Bing (and in a future Combined engine).
- **Demo data.** Made-up appearance days in `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-demo.php` (a few values, scaled from the demo's Google days). Bump `SEARCH_VERSION` so existing demo data gains them.

### Files Scope

- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php`
- `includes/stats/sources/class-seoprostats-source-search-console.php`
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search-import.php`
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search.php`
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-demo.php`
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-api.php`
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-cli.php`
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-abilities.php`
- `packages/core/src/types.ts`
- `packages/core/src/state.ts`
- `packages/wp-admin/src/Search.tsx`
- `packages/wp-admin/src/labels.ts`
- `assets/build/dashboard.js`
- `assets/build/dashboard.asset.php`
- `docs/architecture.md`
- `docs/api/openapi.yaml`
- `README.md`
- `readme.txt`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wp seoprostats search appearance --data=demo --range=30d --format=json` returns rows per appearance with clicks, impressions, CTR, position and comparison changes.
2. On a site connected to Search Console, an import fills `gsc_appearance` for the imported days. A second run doesn't duplicate rows, and undoing the import removes them.
3. The Appearance tab shows for Google and is hidden for Bing. The address keeps the choice.
4. Uninstall drops the new table (smoke test's table list), and visitor pages still run none of the plugin's queries.

title: scripts/demo-site.sh: disposable demo WordPress for runtime and browser checks
body:
## What

Add `scripts/demo-site.sh` (SEO Pro Stats only, not a starter core file): one command that starts a disposable WordPress in Docker on `127.0.0.1` and installs the release build of the current commit. It makes demo data, can copy the demo search data into the live tables, and leaves the site running for runtime and browser checks until `scripts/demo-site.sh down`.

- `scripts/demo-site.sh up [--ref REF] [--live-search] [--post PATH]` prints the URL, a throwaway admin login and the IDs it created.
- `--live-search` copies the demo search tables (`seoprostats_demo_{dict,gsc_pairs,gsc_pages,gsc_queries,gsc_totals,imports}`) into the live ones. Reports that only read live data (the editor's Search queries panel, `/coverage?post=`) then have queries.
- `--post /blog/speed-up-wordpress/` creates a published post at that demo path (permalinks `/blog/%postname%/`), so the editor panel shows the demo page's queries.
- `down` removes the containers, volume and network.

## Why

Checking GH#64 (query coverage) meant hand-writing this setup twice: once for the CLI/REST checks and once for browser screenshots. Each feature that needs runtime or browser evidence on demo data repeats it. `scripts/smoke-test.sh` builds and tears down its own site, and the shared preview site must not be overwritten for agent-only checks (`DEVELOPMENT.md` → Preview site).

## How

- **New file** `scripts/demo-site.sh`. Copy the structure of `scripts/smoke-test.sh`: `parse_args`, `start_site` (MariaDB plus `wordpress:php8.3-apache` on `127.0.0.1::80`, wp-cli in `wordpress:cli-php8.3`), `wp_cli`, the `.htaccess` rules and `cleanup`. Source `scripts/lib/plugin.sh` for `plugin_identity`, and build the zip with `scripts/build-release.sh --ref "$ref" --out "$tmp" --quiet`.
- Use a fixed name prefix (`seoprostats-demo-site`) so `down` finds the containers without state files. Refuse `up` when one already runs.
- Demo data: `wp seoprostats demo make` takes about 4.5 minutes on 400 days, so print progress and say so.
- Live search copy: `wp eval` running `DELETE FROM live; INSERT INTO live SELECT * FROM demo` for each table above. Table names come from `SEOProStats_Schema::table()`; demo tables are `{prefix}seoprostats_demo_*`.
- Login: wp-admin's `auth_redirect()` checks the login cookie, so a `determine_current_user` mu-plugin does not log browsers in. Print `admin` and a random password instead, and keep the site on `127.0.0.1` only.
- Optional: set `{prefix}persisted_preferences` for user 1 to `array('core/edit-post' => array('welcomeGuide' => false))` so screenshots are not blocked by the welcome guide.
- Document it in `DEVELOPMENT.md` → Preview site, next to the throwaway-site bullet.
- Shell rules (`STANDARDS.md`): `local var="$1"`, an explicit `return` in every function, and ShellCheck clean. `scripts/lint.sh` runs ShellCheck on `scripts/`.

### Files Scope

- NEW: `scripts/demo-site.sh`
- EDIT: `DEVELOPMENT.md`

## Acceptance

- `scripts/demo-site.sh up --live-search --post /blog/speed-up-wordpress/` ends by printing a URL. Logged in as the printed admin, `GET /wp-json/seoprostats/v1/coverage?post=<id>` returns 200 with 4 rows and `focus` from the demo.
- `/wp-admin/post.php?post=<id>&action=edit` shows the Search queries panel with queries. `admin.php?page=seoprostats-dashboard#/search?report=opportunities` shows Missing from the page.
- `scripts/demo-site.sh down` leaves no container, volume or network with the prefix (`docker ps -a`, `docker volume ls`, `docker network ls`).
- A second `up` while one runs fails with a clear message.
- `scripts/lint.sh` passes.

## Context

Not a core file. Do not add it to `scripts/core-files.txt`, as it depends on this plugin's demo data and tables. The CLI, REST and browser evidence in PR #67 was gathered with an ad hoc version of this script.

title: Bing: CTR above 100% on rare queries with more clicks than impressions
body:
## Origin

Found while verifying the merged Bing support (#65) on the preview site with live Bing data. About 0.8% of the weekly Bing query rows (50 of 6,593) have more clicks than impressions, for example a rare query with 2 clicks and 1 impression. Search → Rankings then shows that query with a CTR of 200%.

The rows come from Bing as they are. `includes/stats/sources/class-seoprostats-source-bing.php` `weekly()` stores each row's `Clicks` and `Impressions` unchanged, and `SEOProStats_Search_Import::rows()` only adds rows that share a key. Adding can't make clicks exceed impressions, so Bing's own rows already do. Google's data never has this. Site totals are unaffected: all Bing query rows together have 1,774 clicks against 20,340 impressions.

## What

No search report shows a CTR above 100%. Clicks and impressions stay as imported, because they are facts and the totals add up from them; only the derived rate is capped.

## Why

A CTR of 200% looks like broken data on a statistics screen, and in agent answers (REST, WP-CLI, abilities) it can mislead any rule that compares CTRs.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** One central helper does most of it, but the worker must find any other place a CTR is worked out (PHP, SQL and TypeScript) and check the Opportunities rules that compare CTRs.

## How (Approach)

- Central helper: `SEOProStats_Search::metrics()` in `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search.php` (around line 449) sets `'ctr' => $impressions ? round($clicks / $impressions, 4) : 0.0`. Cap it: `min(1.0, round(...))`.
- Find every other CTR worked out from clicks and impressions: `rg -n -i "ctr|/ *.?impressions" includes/stats packages/core/src packages/wp-admin/src`. Check in particular `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-opportunities.php` (`curve()` around line 271 and `pairs_list()`, where the expected-CTR comparison and `potential` use row CTRs) and `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-content.php`. Cap each per-row rate the same way. Sums used for the site's curve are fine as they are, but cap them too if they can exceed 1 on a single rounded position.
- Document it in one sentence in `docs/architecture.md` → Bing Webmaster Tools: Bing sometimes counts more clicks than impressions for a rare query; clicks and impressions are kept as Bing gives them, and CTR is capped at 100%. Add the same to `docs/api/openapi.yaml` where `ctr` is described, if it states a range.
- If a TypeScript formatter or chart works a CTR out from clicks and impressions (`packages/core/src`), cap it there too and rebuild (`npm run build`), committing `assets/build/`.

### Files Scope

- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search.php`
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-opportunities.php`
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-content.php`
- `docs/architecture.md`
- `docs/api/openapi.yaml`
- `packages/core/src/` (only if a CTR is worked out there)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every `ctr` returned by the REST routes `search`, `opportunities` and `content` (with `engine=bing` and `engine=google`) is between 0 and 1. To check without live Bing data, temporarily give one demo Bing row more clicks than impressions (`wp db query` on `{prefix}seoprostats_demo_gsc_queries`, engine 2), then run `wp seoprostats search --engine=bing --data=demo --format=json` and check that query's `ctr` is 1. Restore the demo data afterwards with `wp seoprostats demo make`.
2. Clicks and impressions in the answers are unchanged (totals equal the sums of stored rows).
3. `composer install && scripts/lint.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh --php 7.4` pass; put the results in the PR (AGENTS.md: checks run locally for now).

## Context & Decisions

- Don't change the import: clamping clicks to impressions there would change the totals.
- The repository is private until launch and is published whole: use made-up examples only and never name a real site or its queries (AGENTS.md → Write as if public).
- Out of scope: chart axis rounding (#66), the Combined engine (#68).

title: SEO loop: experiments — record a change and measure it against unchanged pages
body:
Part of the SEO decision loop (#61). Design: `docs/seo-loop.md` → 1. Experiments.

## Goal

Record a change and what it is expected to do (page or pages, metric, direction, threshold, review date), then measure it: the same number of days before and after, against comparable pages that did not change, with search engine updates and other changes named as confounders. Suggest keep, revise, undo or inconclusive; a person or agent decides. Experiments appear on the timeline.

## Why

Changes are logged and search and visit data are imported, but nobody checks weeks later whether a change worked. This closes the loop on the site itself.

### Files Scope

- NEW: `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-experiments.php`
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php`
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-changes.php`

- `packages/core/src/state.ts`
- `docs/api/openapi.yaml`

- `docs/seo-loop.md`
- `README.md`
- `readme.txt`
- `todo/PLANS.md`
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh`

Schema v8 adds `experiments`; Changes gains kind 81 `experiment`; the smoke test adds `EXPLAIN` of the new reads.

## Reference pattern

- Report class with cache and engine handling: `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-opportunities.php` (`report()`, cache key with the newest import).
- Notes written into the change log: `SEOProStats_Changes::annotate()` and `delete_note()`.
- Confounders: `SEOProStats_Changes::updates_between()`, `on_pages()`.
- Visits from search per page: `SEOProStats_Rollup::SEARCH_LANDING` in `daily`; conversions per entry page: `SEOProStats_Conversions::by_entry()`.

## Acceptance

- Table `experiments` with keys `status_review`, `path_id`, `start`; every new read uses an index (smoke test `EXPLAIN`).
- Windows of 7, 14, 28, 56 or 84 days; Google and Bing windows as in the design; `running` until search data reaches the review day.
- Comparison group of unchanged pages; effect relative to it; `compared: false` without one; noise band from the group's own pages; minimum data; confounders listed.
- Decisions freeze the measurement in `meta.measured`.
- REST `experiments` routes, WP-CLI `experiments`, abilities, Search → Experiments tab, demo experiments of each result.
- Wording says "associated with" unless the comparison group supports more.

## Verification

- `composer install && scripts/lint.sh`, `npm run --silent typecheck`, `npm run --silent build`
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh --php 7.4`
- Preview site (`scripts/preview-site.sh`) with demo data: Search → Experiments lists the demo experiments with numbers; `wp seoprostats experiments list --data=demo`.

title: Keep our own lines in core files inside the spst-own sync blocks
body:
## What

Move SEO Pro Stats' own lines in three core files into the `spst-own` marked blocks that the starter adds, so `scripts/sync-core.sh` keeps them instead of deleting them on every sync.

**Blocked by:** wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding#398 (adds the `{css}-own:start` / `{css}-own:end` blocks to core files and teaches `sync-core.sh` to keep their contents). blocked-by:wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding#398

## Why

The shop-test lines below are this plugin's own. Every core sync so far has deleted them and they had to be put back by hand. If they are missed, the shop-test fixture ships in release zips and the release step disappears. `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` also reports these three files as `differs` for good, which hides real drift.

## How

1. After starter #398 merges, run `scripts/sync-core.sh` from the starter as usual (`DEVELOPMENT.md` → core files). It brings in the empty `spst-own` blocks (the starter's `wps-own` renamed by `plugin_map`) and the updated `sync-core.sh`. The sync will still drop the lines below this one time, because they are not inside blocks yet.
2. Put the plugin's own lines back, inside the blocks, with the same wording:
   - `.distignore`: the two lines currently after `/scripts`:
     `# Disposable shop-test fixture: never install it as a production must-use plugin.` and `/scripts/shop-test-mu.php`.
   - `DEVELOPMENT.md`: the checks-table row `| Shop test (when present) | ... |` (currently after the Smoke test row), and the paragraph that starts "The shop test defaults to PHP 8.2 and latest WordPress and shop versions." through its end. If the starter's block sits after the table rather than inside it, keep the row in the table only if the block allows it; otherwise turn it into a sentence in the block. Keep `scripts/lint.sh` "runs the first seven" accurate.
   - `RELEASING.md`: the step-2 lines "When `scripts/shop-test.sh` exists, run it before release if purchases code or a supported shop has changed since the last check, including `scripts/shop-test.sh --php 7.4 --wp 6.2`. Keep the tested shop versions and any compatibility skips in the pull request's verification results."
3. Use the exact marker text and positions the starter ships; do not invent new markers.
4. `changelog.txt` and `README.md` → Unreleased: one Developers line only if the sync's own changelog entry does not already cover it.

Reference: the "How" section of starter #398 for marker names and positions; `scripts/sync-core.sh` `sync_file()` after the sync.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.distignore`
- EDIT: `DEVELOPMENT.md`
- EDIT: `RELEASING.md`
- EDIT: other core files and `scripts/sync-core.sh`, only as written by `scripts/sync-core.sh`
- EDIT (maybe): `changelog.txt`, `README.md`

## Verify

- `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` reports no `differs` for `.distignore`, `DEVELOPMENT.md` and `RELEASING.md`.
- Running `scripts/sync-core.sh` again changes nothing (`git status` clean), and the shop-test lines are still there.
- `scripts/build-release.sh`: the zip does not contain `scripts/shop-test-mu.php` (already true because `/scripts` is excluded; the line documents the intent).
- `composer install && scripts/lint.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` pass; put the results in the PR (GitHub Actions do not run on this repository yet, see `AGENTS.md`).

title: Move here: import history and settings from other statistics plugins, with Plugins screen notices
body:
Phase 7 of `todo/PLANS.md` ("move from other statistics plugins"). A site switching to SEO Pro Stats keeps its history and settings. Then, with guidance, it removes the old plugin and everything it left behind.

## Goal

1. **Detection by data, not just by plugin**: a source is listed whenever its data is on the site (its tables, options, or for Jetpack a live WordPress.com connection with the Stats module), whether the plugin is active, inactive or already deleted.
2. **Import page** (Settings → Import): for each source, a dry run (days, date range, rows, overlap with other sources, settings that would change), then import with progress, and undo per import.
3. **History**: daily totals and top lists (pages, referrers, countries, devices, browsers, systems, where the source has them) go into `daily` with an import id.
4. **No double counting**: each day is filled by one source only. Days SEO Pro Stats recorded itself are never imported over. When several sources cover the same days, the dry run shows the overlap and the owner picks which source fills those days (#109).
5. **Settings**: equivalent settings (excluded roles, excluded IP addresses, Do Not Track, retention) are filled only where ours still have their defaults, and shown in the dry run first.
6. **Guided removal**: after an import, the owner is asked to check the imported days (a comparison with the source's own totals and a link to the reports for that range). Then they deactivate and delete the plugin, with its own delete-data-on-uninstall setting turned on first if it has one, or use our **Remove leftover data** action once the plugin is inactive or gone (#109, #110).
7. **Plugins screen and notices** (#110): while a source has data that is not imported, or leftovers remain, a notice and a note on its row say what to do next, with links to the Import page. The notice goes away only when the plugin and its data are both gone.

## Owner decisions (2026-10-08)

- **Run side by side.** SEO Pro Stats keeps collecting while other statistics plugins stay active. So no statistics plugin goes in `REPLACES` (that would pause our tracking, `includes/class-seoprostats-feature.php`). The notices come from our own class instead.
- **Remove leftovers on request.** SEO Pro Stats may delete another plugin's leftover tables and options, but only through the explicit, confirmed **Remove leftover data** action, and only once that plugin is inactive or deleted. This is a plugin-own exception to `STANDARDS.md` → Structure ("never writes or deletes the other plugin's options"), recorded in `AGENTS.md`. Imports themselves still only read.
- **Jetpack is built from its open-source code**, without a test site. The owner will invite people who use Jetpack Stats to test it (#111).

## Children

Every child after the first is blocked by #109.

1. #109: engine, data detection, dry run, overlap choice, import, undo, check-after-import, Remove leftover data, Import tab, REST, WP-CLI, abilities, and Burst Statistics. `tier:thinking`
2. #110: Plugins screen and admin notices through the whole cycle (import, check, deactivate and delete, remove leftovers). `tier:standard`
3. #111: Jetpack Stats through the site's Jetpack connection. `tier:thinking`
4. #112: Koko Analytics and Statify. `tier:standard`
5. #113: WP Statistics and Independent Analytics. `tier:standard`
6. #114: Slimstat and Matomo for WordPress. `tier:thinking`

Plugins that only send data to Google Analytics keep no history on the site, so they are out of scope. A Google Analytics import would be an outside source under #37.

## Rules every child follows

- **Private by design** (`docs/architecture.md` → Collection): import only counts. Never copy IP addresses (raw or hashed), visitor or user IDs, user agent strings, or anything typed into forms, even when the source keeps them. Aggregate in SQL and read only the aggregate.
- **Visitor pages pay nothing**: detection, import and cleanup run only in wp-admin, WP-CLI, REST or cron, never on a visitor page. Cache detection in a non-autoloaded option, refreshed at most daily or when the Import tab or Plugins screen opens.
- **Imports only read.** The only writes to another plugin's data are those of Remove leftover data, which needs confirmation, deletes exactly what it lists, and is refused while that plugin is active.
- **Indexed reads**: read source tables by their indexed date column, in day batches under a time budget (`SEOProStats_Feature::more_time()`). Our own new queries on `daily` must use an index, checked by `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (`scripts/smoke-queries.php`).
- **Verify each source on a real install** of its current version (`scripts/demo-site.sh` or `scripts/preview-site.sh`, `wp plugin install <slug> --activate`, create traffic, `SHOW CREATE TABLE`, and list its options with `wp option list --search='<prefix>*'`). Jetpack is the exception (#111). Support each table layout still found on sites, and name the versions checked in the adapter's docblock.
- **Verify plugin slugs** with `wp plugin search` or the WordPress.org plugin API.
- **Write as if public** (`AGENTS.md`): naming the plugins we import from is part of the feature. Describe them in our own words, and never copy their code.

## Verification (each child)

- `composer install && scripts/lint.sh`, `npm run --silent typecheck`, `npm run --silent build` when `packages/` changes
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (Docker), with results pasted in the PR (Actions are off for this private repository, see `AGENTS.md`)
- On a demo site with the source plugin and some traffic: the dry run shows the counts; import fills the reports for those days; a second run adds nothing; undo removes exactly those rows. After deactivating the plugin, Remove leftover data deletes exactly the listed tables and options, and the notice goes away.

title: Move here: import engine, overlap rules, leftover cleanup, Settings → Import tab and Burst Statistics
body:
Parent: #108. Read it first for the goal, the owner's decisions and the rules every child follows. This is the first child: the engine, the Import tab, removing leftovers, and the first source, Burst Statistics. Every other child adds an adapter on top of it.

## Goal

1. The owner opens SEO Pro Stats → Settings → **Import** and sees Burst Statistics listed whenever its data is on the site (plugin active, inactive or deleted with its tables left), with its date range and day count.
2. They run a dry run, import, and see those days in the reports.
3. The tab then asks them to check the imported days, deactivate and delete Burst, and finally offers **Remove leftover data** for whatever the plugin left behind.

## Design

### Source adapters

An abstract `SEOProStats_Migrate_Source` with these methods:

- `KEY` (the `imports.source` value, such as `burst-statistics`), `NAME`, `SLUGS` (plugin folders).
- `detect()`: whether its data is present, judged from its tables and options (not only from the plugin being installed); plugin state (active, inactive, not installed); first and last day. Cheap, with no full scans.
- `days($from, $to)`: per day, the site totals plus the top values per dimension the source has, mapped to `SEOProStats_Rollup::DIMS` (`page`, `source`, `country`, `device`, `browser`, `os`, `entry`, `utm_*` where present). Paths go through the dictionary the way the processor stores them; countries use the processor's encoding.
- `totals($from, $to)`: the source's own pageview and visitor totals for a range, for the check after import.
- `settings()`: a map of its options to our setting keys, with a converter for each.
- `leftovers()`: exactly what it leaves on the site. Its tables (with this site's `$wpdb->prefix`), options (known names, or a prefix only it uses, checked on a real install), cron hooks, transients, user meta keys, and any upload folder. Only what is present right now.
- `uninstall_setting()`: the plugin's own "delete data when uninstalled" option, if it has one: key, label, and where to find it in its settings.

A registry `SEOProStats_Migrate::sources()` that other children extend by adding one class, plus a `seoprostats_migrate_sources` filter.

### Imported days

- They live in `daily`. The schema moves to v14 and adds `import_id int unsigned NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` to `daily`. Undo deletes `WHERE day BETWEEN … AND import_id = %d` in batches, using the `(day,dim,val)` primary-key prefix.
- Each run writes an `imports` row: `source` = adapter `KEY`, `day_from`, `day_to`, `rows_added`, and `meta` holding the version read, settings changed, and days skipped with the reason.
- **Rollup must not erase imported rows.** `SEOProStats_Rollup` deletes a day with `DELETE FROM %i WHERE day = %s` (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-rollup.php:212`, and the `SEARCH_LANDING` delete near line 296). Restrict both deletes to `import_id = 0`.

### No double counting

Each day is filled by one source.

- **Our own days win.** Import only days before the first day SEO Pro Stats recorded itself (the first `daily` day with `dim = 0 AND import_id = 0`, or today when there is none). Other plugins keep running side by side, so their later days are never needed.
- **The same source twice.** Days the source already filled are skipped, so a second run adds 0 and a later run is safe.
- **Several sources.** A day another source's import already filled is skipped, and the dry run lists those days. When two or more sources that are not imported yet share days, the dry run shows the shared range and the tab asks which one to use for those days (default: the one with more pageviews over the shared days). That source imports first; the others then fill only the days left. To change the choice later, undo the import and run again; the tab says so.
- Days are whole days. On our first day the site's own count starts at install time; document that.

### Check after import

The finished import shows the source's own totals (`totals()`) beside the imported totals for the same range, plus a link to the Overview for that range (each section's view is in the address, #24). Then come the next steps:

1. Check the days.
2. Turn on the plugin's own delete-data setting if it has one (`uninstall_setting()`), then deactivate and delete it. Show a Deactivate link like core's, for people who can.
3. Or, once it is inactive or deleted, use Remove leftover data.

### Remove leftover data

`SEOProStats_Migrate::cleanup($source, $dry_run)`.

- It lists `leftovers()` and deletes exactly that list after confirmation in the tab, or `--yes` in WP-CLI.
- **Refused** while the plugin is active on this site or network-wide. Needs `delete_plugins` and `manage_options`.
- Tables are dropped with `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS %i`, one per listed name. Options with `delete_option()`. Cron hooks with `wp_clear_scheduled_hook()`.
- On multisite it acts on this site only, and lists network-wide leftovers without deleting them.
- It never touches our imported rows. It cannot be undone, so the confirmation says so and suggests a database backup.
- It writes one site `changes` row ("leftover data of {plugin} removed").
- This is the owner's exception to `STANDARDS.md` → Structure. Add one line under "Rules for any change" in `AGENTS.md`: SEO Pro Stats may delete another statistics plugin's leftovers only through this confirmed action, and only while that plugin is inactive.

### Runs

- WP-CLI runs to the end. The admin and REST start a cron job that works in batches of days under the existing 20-second budget and a lock, following `SEOProStats_Search_Import` (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search-import.php`: `start()`, `finish()`, `undo()`, lock, budget). The tab polls for progress.
- **Undo**: `DELETE /imports/{id}` (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-api.php:469`, `undo_import()` near line 960) currently calls `SEOProStats_Search_Import::undo()`. Route it by `imports.source` so migration imports undo through `SEOProStats_Migrate::undo()`.
- **Timeline**: one site `changes` row on the import's last day ("statistics imported from {plugin}"), using an existing kind and source if one fits (`SEOProStats_Changes::KINDS`).

### Settings and the first adapter

- **Settings**: the dry run lists each mapped setting with the source's value and ours. The import fills only settings still at their default, and never writes the source's options.
- **Burst Statistics** adapter: read its tables, options and uninstall behaviour from a real install of the current version, and name the version in the docblock.

### Files Scope

- NEW: `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-migrate.php` (registry, detection cache, run, undo, overlap, cleanup)
- NEW: `includes/stats/migrate/class-seoprostats-migrate-source.php`
- NEW: `includes/stats/migrate/class-seoprostats-migrate-burst.php`
- NEW: `includes/admin/class-seoprostats-import-tab.php` (tab through `seoprostats_admin_tabs`, like `includes/admin/class-seoprostats-connections-tab.php`)
- NEW: `admin/js/seoprostats-import.js` (like `admin/js/seoprostats-connections.js`)
- `includes/class-seoprostats-setup.php` (load the tab in `admin()`)
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php` (v14)
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-rollup.php`
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-api.php` (`GET /migrate`, `POST /migrate/{source}` with `dry_run` and `prefer`, `POST /migrate/{source}/cleanup` with `dry_run`, undo routing)
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-cli.php` (`wp seoprostats migrate list|run <source> [--dry-run] [--prefer=<source>] [--from] [--to]|imports|undo --id|cleanup <source> [--dry-run] [--yes]`)
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-abilities.php` (read: sources, dry run, leftovers; write: import, following `seoprostats/targets-import`. Cleanup stays out of abilities: people only.)
- `AGENTS.md` (the leftovers exception, one line)
- `uninstall.php` (new options, transients and cron hook)
- `docs/architecture.md` (new section "Moving from other statistics plugins": detection, overlap, check, cleanup; `daily.import_id` in Storage), `docs/api/openapi.yaml`
- `README.md` (feature line, the Read Me tab), `readme.txt` (FAQ: bringing history across, removing the old plugin). Check `context/keywords.md` first for the wording people search for.
- `scripts/smoke-queries.php` / `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (the undo delete and the first-own-day and overlap queries use an index)

## Reference pattern

- Import runs, lock, budget, undo and `imports` rows: `SEOProStats_Search_Import`
- Settings tab with its own script: `SEOProStats_Connections_Tab` and `admin/js/seoprostats-connections.js`
- CLI `imports` and `undo`: `SEOProStats_CLI::imports_command()` (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-cli.php:3298`)
- Deactivate link that comes back: `SEOProStats_Replaced_Plugins::deactivate_url()` (`admin/includes/class-replaced-plugins.php`)

## Acceptance

- **Detection**: Burst Statistics is listed while its data is present, whether the plugin is active, inactive or deleted, and not listed once its data is gone.
- **Dry run**: shows the date range, days, rows per dimension, overlap with other sources and our own days, settings that would change, and writes nothing.
- **Import**:
  - Fills `daily` only for days before our first day and not filled by another import.
  - Overview, Pages, Referrers, Countries and Devices show those days.
  - A second run adds 0 rows.
  - Undo removes exactly that import's rows.
  - A rollup over an imported range leaves imported rows in place.
- **Overlap**: two sources sharing days, imported one after the other, never fill a day twice. The `prefer` choice decides which fills the shared days.
- **Check**: the finished import shows source totals beside imported totals and the next steps.
- **Cleanup**:
  - Refused while Burst is active.
  - Once Burst is inactive or deleted, the dry run lists its tables, options and cron hooks; the real run deletes exactly those, and detection then no longer lists Burst.
- **Privacy**: only counts are read. No IP address, visitor hash or user agent leaves the source tables.
- **Visitor pages**: nothing runs on them. Detection is cached.

## Verification

- `composer install && scripts/lint.sh`, `npm run --silent typecheck`, `npm run --silent build`
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (Docker), with results in the PR
- Demo site:
  1. `wp plugin install burst-statistics --activate` (check the slug first) and open front-end pages logged out.
  2. `wp seoprostats migrate run burst-statistics --dry-run`, then run it, run it again (0 rows), and `undo --id`; then import again.
  3. `cleanup burst-statistics --dry-run` while active (refused). Deactivate, then `cleanup --dry-run` and `cleanup --yes`.
  4. Check with `wp db query "SHOW TABLES LIKE '%burst%'"` that nothing is left.
- Screenshots of the Import tab in each state (`workflows/ui-verification.md`)

<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: Move here: notices from import to removal (Plugins screen and SEO Pro Stats screens), running side by side
body:
Parent: #108. Read it first for the goal, the owner's decisions and the rules. blocked-by: #109 (the foundation child, which provides the source registry, cached detection, import state, cleanup and the Import tab).

## Goal

From the moment another statistics plugin's data is found until the plugin **and** its leftover data are gone, the owner sees one clear next step, with a link:

| State | When | Message and links |
|---|---|---|
| `import` | Its data has days not imported yet (before our first day, not filled by another import) | SEO Pro Stats can bring in {plugin}'s history ({first} to {last}). Link: **Import its history** (Import tab, source selected) |
| `check` | Nothing left to import; the plugin is still active | Check the imported days, then deactivate and delete {plugin}. If it has a delete-data setting, turn that on first (named from the adapter's `uninstall_setting()`). Links: **Check the import**, **Deactivate** |
| `remove` | The plugin is inactive or deleted; leftovers remain | {plugin} left data on the site. Links: **Delete {plugin}** (when installed, using its own uninstall), **Remove leftover data** (Import tab, cleanup for that source) |
| none | Plugin and data gone | Nothing |

A plugin that started after SEO Pro Stats has no days to import, so it goes straight to `check`: SEO Pro Stats already records these days.

## Design

- **Run side by side (owner's decision).** Do not add `REPLACES` or `'replaces'` to the tracking switch. That would pause our collection (`includes/class-seoprostats-feature.php`). The core `admin/includes/class-replaced-plugins.php` stays unused for statistics plugins and unedited (it is a core file).
- New class `includes/admin/class-seoprostats-migrate-notices.php`. It reads only the cached detection and import state from #109, so it never scans tables on a screen load.
  - **Plugins screen** (`load-plugins.php`, for people who can `activate_plugins`):
    - A note under each installed source's row (`after_plugin_row`, the same markup as core's update notes: `tr.plugin-update-tr` → `notice inline notice-info notice-alt`, joined to the row the way core does it).
    - A top notice listing every source not in the none state, including deleted plugins whose data remains (they have no row).
  - **SEO Pro Stats's own screens** (statistics and settings): the same top notice, so it is seen without visiting Plugins. Not on other admin screens.
  - **Hide** is per person, per `slug:state`, through user meta and a nonce'd `admin-post` action. Use the same pattern as `SEOProStats_Replaced_Plugins::hide()`. A source shows again when its state changes.
  - The Deactivate link uses core's plugins.php deactivate URL, as `SEOProStats_Replaced_Plugins::plugins_deactivate_url()` builds it. Delete uses core's delete-selected flow. Both show only with the matching capability.
- **Jetpack** (#111): its row is Jetpack's (or the standalone Jetpack Stats plugin's). In `check`, the step is "turn off the Stats module in Jetpack" (Jetpack → Settings) instead of deactivating Jetpack, which does other jobs. Take the wording from the adapter (an optional `removal_step()` on the adapter base, added here if #109 did not add it).
- Copy: plain and short, in WordPress's tone. Check `context/keywords.md` for the words people use ("import", "migrate", "switch from").

### Files Scope

- NEW: `includes/admin/class-seoprostats-migrate-notices.php`
- `includes/class-seoprostats-setup.php` (load it in `admin()`)
- `includes/stats/migrate/class-seoprostats-migrate-source.php` (only if `removal_step()` is needed)
- `uninstall.php` (the hide user meta)
- `README.md` (feature line), `readme.txt` (FAQ)
- `docs/architecture.md` (moving section: notices and states)

## Reference pattern

`admin/includes/class-replaced-plugins.php`: `row_note()`, `row_note_style()`, `notice()`, `hide()`, `plugins_deactivate_url()`. Reuse the patterns, not the class.

## Acceptance

- Burst Statistics active with history: row note and top notice in `import`. After import: `check`, with Deactivate. After deactivation: `remove`, with Delete and Remove leftover data. After cleanup: nothing.
- Burst deleted without its data deleted: the top notice shows `remove`, though there is no row.
- SEO Pro Stats keeps collecting the whole time. No statistics plugin is in `REPLACES`.
- Hide hides only the listed states. Nothing is shown to people without `activate_plugins`. No source table is queried on page load.

## Verification

- `composer install && scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (Docker), with results in the PR
- Demo site with Burst Statistics: screenshots of the Plugins screen and the SEO Pro Stats screen in each state (`workflows/ui-verification.md`, never a full-page screenshot)

title: Move here: Jetpack Stats history, built from Jetpack's open-source code (tested later by invited users)
body:
Parent: #108. Read it first for the goal, the owner's decisions and the rules. blocked-by: #109 (the foundation child, which provides the adapter base, `daily.import_id`, overlap handling, cleanup, the Import tab, REST and WP-CLI).

## Goal

A site that used Jetpack Stats brings its history across: daily views and visitors, top posts and pages, referrers and countries per day, for as far back as WordPress.com gives them.

## Built without a test site (owner's decision)

The owner has no site running Jetpack. Build the adapter from Jetpack's open-source code and WordPress.com's public API docs. The owner will invite people who use Jetpack Stats to test it. The PR can merge once lint and the smoke test pass and the code matches the sources below. Do not add mocks, recorded responses or test-only hooks. Make it easy for a tester to report back instead (see "Tester support").

## Sources to read (public)

- Jetpack monorepo: `Automattic/jetpack` (branch `trunk`), read with `gh api repos/Automattic/jetpack/contents/<path>`:
  - `projects/packages/stats/src/class-wpcom-stats.php`: `Automattic\Jetpack\Stats\WPCOM_Stats`.
    - Methods: `get_visits()`, `get_top_posts()`, `get_referrers()`, `get_views_by_country()`, `get_stats()`.
    - `build_endpoint()` gives `/sites/{Jetpack_Options::get_option('id')}/stats/{resource}`.
    - `fetch_remote_stats()` calls `Automattic\Jetpack\Connection\Client::wpcom_json_api_request_as_blog( $endpoint, '1.1', array( 'timeout' => 20 ) )` and maps token errors to `site_not_connected`.
    - **`fetch_stats()` caches every answer in a `jetpack_restapi_stats_cache_*` transient.** Calling it once per day of history would leave hundreds of transients. Call the connection client the same way `fetch_remote_stats()` does, so nothing is cached in Jetpack's name. If the client class or method is missing, show "update Jetpack" rather than falling back.
  - `projects/packages/stats/src/class-main.php`: `should_track()` tracks only when the site is connected (`Connection_Manager::is_connected()`) and the `stats` module is active (`Modules::is_active('stats')`). Use the same two checks for detection.
  - `projects/plugins/stats/composer.json`: the standalone Jetpack Stats plugin's slug is `jetpack-stats`. The full plugin is `jetpack`; check its slug the same way.
- The WordPress.com REST API 1.1 docs linked from those methods' `@link` tags (`/sites/$site/stats/visits`, `top-posts`, `referrers`, `country-views`): parameters such as `unit`, `quantity`, `date`, `period`, `max`, and the response shapes. Write down in the adapter's docblock which parameters and fields you rely on, with the Jetpack version (`projects/packages/stats` changelog) you read.

## Design

- **Detection**: Jetpack or Jetpack Stats is installed and the site is connected (the history lives on WordPress.com, not in the site's tables). When it is not connected, the tab says to connect Jetpack first. Once Jetpack is gone, the history can no longer be imported, so the notices (#110) ask to import before removing it.
- **Runs**: remote requests only in the cron job or WP-CLI, in day batches under the budget. Back off on errors and rate limits. The `imports` row keeps the last day done, so a run continues where it stopped.
- **Mapping**:
  - Views → `daily.pageviews`.
  - Visitors → `visitors`. Jetpack has no visits, so `visits` = visitors. Note the definitions in `docs/architecture.md`.
  - Posts and pages → `page` (each post ID's current path, through the dictionary; skip IDs that no longer exist).
  - Referrers → `source` (host).
  - Countries → `country`.
  - No device, browser or system data. Search terms are mostly hidden, so they are left out.

Two follow-ups to the Search Appearance report (#70, PR #105):

The CLI is one of the three agent interfaces (REST, WP-CLI, abilities). Demo data is how people preview a report, and identical ratios hide the comparison the report exists to show.

## What

The Settings table in the Import tab's dry run (`admin/js/seoprostats-import.js`, `drawPlan()`) is hard to read. Every column after the first is marked numeric, so text values are right-aligned, and the first column ("Its setting → our label") wraps into a narrow strip. The owner also cannot choose which settings an import carries over: it fills every setting of ours that is still at its default.

## Do

- **Choice**: each setting the import would change has a checkbox, ticked by default. Settings it would not change (already the same, or changed by the owner) show why, with the checkbox disabled. The Import button sends only the ticked settings.
- **Server**: `SEOProStats_Migrate` applies only the chosen settings. title: A/B tests 1/4: blocks, editor, registry and the site's variant swap (#29)
body:
## What

Part 1 of #29 (A/B testing of blocks): the blocks, the editor, the test registry and the site's variant swap. No statistics yet: part 2 collects which variant was shown.

**Names.** SEO Pro Stats already has **Experiments** (GH#73: a change, its expected effect and review date; `experiments` table, `/experiments`, `wp seoprostats experiments`). These tests are therefore **A/B tests** everywhere: blocks `seoprostats/ab-test` and `seoprostats/ab-variant`, table `ab_tests`, REST `/ab-tests`, `wp seoprostats ab-tests`, the dimension `variant`, and an "A/B tests" section. Never "experiments".

### Editor (block editor)

- An **A/B test** toolbar button on every block and on a multi-block selection wraps the selection in `seoprostats/ab-test`, with variants `seoprostats/ab-variant` (inner blocks: any block type). Variant A holds the original and Variant B starts as a copy.
- A **variant dropdown** in the test block's toolbar ("Variant A ▾") picks which variant shows and is edited in the canvas. The others are hidden, not removed. It is keyboard reachable and labelled.
- **Sidebar** (`InspectorControls`): the test name (default from the post title), status (draft, running, paused, ended), the goal(s) it is judged by (from Goals), and variants. For each variant: a label (renamable; the slug `variant-a`… stays once set), add (blank or duplicate), remove, reorder, and a weight (equal by default).
- Each test has a stable random ID in its attributes. A duplicate ID in one post is renewed on save.
- Site editor templates and synced patterns: no button there yet, and the UI says so.

### Registry

- On `save_post`, parse the post's blocks and upsert `ab_tests` (test ID, post ID, name, variants as JSON: slug, label, weight; status, goals, started, ended). Tests removed from a post are marked removed, not deleted, so data stays readable. This happens only on save, never on a visitor page. Use the next free schema version.

### On the site

- Render the control (Variant A, or the winner once set) as normal markup and the other variants in `<template>` elements. Crawlers, no-JS visitors, feeds and page caches then see one variant.
- A tiny inline script after a running test picks a variant by weight for that page load before paint and swaps the template in. It sets `data-spst-ab="<test>:<variant>"` on the test's wrapper for part 2. It runs no query, option read or remote request (everything is in the block's attributes).
- Draft, paused and ended tests print only the control or winner, with no script and no templates.

## Files

- NEW: `blocks/ab-test/block.json`, `blocks/ab-variant/block.json` (or registered in PHP; follow how the plugin registers other editor code)
- NEW: `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-ab-tests.php` (registry on save, render callbacks, inline swap script)
- NEW: `packages/wp-admin/src/ab-test/` (editor: blocks, toolbar button via `editor.BlockEdit` filter + `BlockControls`, sidebar), as its own webpack entry (pattern: `packages/wp-admin/src/editor.tsx` and `webpack.config.js`)
- EDIT: `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php` (`ab_tests`), `uninstall.php`, `webpack.config.js`, the class that enqueues `editor` (search `seoprostats-editor`), rebuilt `assets/build/`
- EDIT: `docs/architecture.md`, `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `todo/PLANS.md`

## Check

- `composer install && scripts/lint.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` pass. Visitor pages, including one with a running test, make no plugin queries (add a page with a running test to the smoke test's pages if it has a hook for that; otherwise check with the disposable site's query log).
- Editor (Chromium, 1440 and 390 wide): start a test from a paragraph, a button and a group; switch variants from the toolbar; rename, add, remove and reweight; it is keyboard-only throughout. Save, and `ab_tests` has the row.
- Logged out: the page source shows one variant plus `<template>`s. Over 50 loads, the split matches the weights. A screenshot right after load shows no flicker. There are no cookies or storage. A paused or ended test prints only the control or winner. A bot user agent with no JS sees only the control.

title: A/B tests 2/4: collect each page load's variant privately (#29)
body:
Blocked by: #133

## What

Part 2 of #29: collect which A/B test variant each page load showed, privately. It depends on part 1 (blocks, `ab_tests`, and the swap script setting `data-spst-ab="<test>:<variant>"`).

- **Tracker** (`packages/tracker/src/index.ts`): the pageview carries the test:variant pairs shown on the page (read from `[data-spst-ab]` when the pageview is sent). Clicks inside a variant carry it. Keep the tracker under its size budget.
- **Collector and processor**: store exposures by page load (pageview key, test ID, variant slug, day, session) in a small `ab_exposures` table, indexed for per-test reports by day (`EXPLAIN` with the smoke test). Use the next free schema version. Retention follows the pageviews' retention.
- **Mixed visits**: a visit that saw more than one variant of the same test is counted as mixed and left out of comparisons (part 3 reports the count). Work this out in the report from exposures, not by changing assignment.
- **One variant per visit** (opt-in, off by default): a setting under Settings → Tracking, explained as browser storage that privacy law treats like cookies. When on, the swap script keeps the visit's variant in `sessionStorage`. When off, nothing is stored in the browser.

body:
Parent: #37 (outside data sources). After the backlinks child (links table and Search → Backlinks). DataForSEO is the first paid provider; it fills the same `links` table and adds tracked keyword positions.

## What

- **Connection** (Settings → Connections, `POST /connections/dataforseo`, `wp seoprostats connect dataforseo`): the owner's API login and password, stored encrypted as the other connections are (`SEOProStats_Connections`), checked with DataForSEO's free account request, which also shows the balance. Kept apart from the search engines' import job: providers are their own list (`SEOProStats_Connections::PROVIDERS`), so the search import never treats them as engines.
- **Monthly spend limit**: every request's cost (DataForSEO returns it) is added to the month's total; a limit the owner sets (default $5 a month) stops requests until the next month. The tab and `doctor` show spent and left. Requests come only from cron or the owner's action.
- **Backlinks** weekly: the site's live backlinks (top by rank, default 1,000) and those lost since the last run, into `links` with `found` DataForSEO, the referring page's rank as authority, first and last seen and lost as DataForSEO gives them; summary (referring domains, backlinks, rank) kept in the connection state. New and lost referring sites become the same `backlink_new` / `backlink_lost` changes.
- **Tracked positions**: the site's search targets (Search → Targets) are checked weekly in Google's results (DataForSEO SERP API, the site's country and language, desktop and mobile) into a new `serp` table (schema: query, engine, device, day, position, the site's page, result features). A move of 3 or more places, or into or out of the top 10, is a `rank_move` change. Targets shows the tracked position next to Search Console's average.
- REST, WP-CLI (`wp seoprostats dataforseo status|run|spend`), OpenAPI, docs, README, readme.txt, changelog.
