title: Backlinks: verified referrers, the links table, Search → Backlinks and timeline markers
body:
Parent: #37 (outside data sources). First child after Search Console and Bing: backlinks from the site's own data, with no outside service, so every site gets them.

## What

- **Schema v18 `links`** (`docs/architecture.md` → Storage already names it): one row per referring page (`path_id` 0, the page checked) and one per link found on it to one of the site's pages. Columns: `id`, `lkey` (8-byte key of the source address and target page, unique), `source_host_id` (`DICT_HOST`), `source_url_id` (new dictionary kind), `path_id` (target page, `DICT_PATH`), `anchor_id` (`DICT_LABEL`), `rel` (bits: nofollow, sponsored, ugc), `found` (bits: 1 referrer, later 2 DataForSEO…), `status` (0 checked with no link, 1 live, 2 lost), `first_seen`, `last_seen`, `lost`, `checked`, `misses`, `authority` (a provider's, 0 none). Keys for the job (`status`, `checked`) and the reports (`first_seen`, `lost`, host, page). Demo tables too.
- **Verification job** (`SEOProStats_Backlinks`, daily cron, 20-second budget, never on a visitor page): candidates are visits from the Referral channel in the last days (sessions by `started`), each referring page once; it fetches the page with `wp_safe_remote_get()` (private addresses refused, 5 s timeout, at most 1 MB, an honest user agent naming the plugin and site), reads the `<a href>` links to the site's hosts with their text and `rel`, and records them. Host-only referrers (most browsers send only the origin) check the referring site's home page. Pages are re-checked weekly, oldest first; a link missing on two checks in a row, or a page gone (404/410), is lost. Fetch errors don't count as a miss.
- **Settings**: on by default under Settings → Data ("Check pages that send visitors for links", with what it fetches and sends); off stops the job.
- **Changes**: new kinds `backlink_new` and `backlink_lost` (group seo), one change per referring site and day with the pages in `meta`, so they line up with traffic on the timeline.
- **Reports**: `GET /backlinks` (`kind`: links, domains, pages, lost; period filter on first seen / lost), `wp seoprostats backlinks [<kind>]` and `wp seoprostats backlinks check`, ability `seoprostats/backlinks`, OpenAPI and core types. Dashboard: **Search → Backlinks** tab: tiles (referring sites, live links, new and lost in the period), tables of links (source, target page, anchor, rel, first and last seen, how found), referring sites (with their visits in the period from the daily `source` summaries) and lost links. Demo data has backlinks.
- Fix found while planning: the daily cron (`SEOProStats_Collection::DAILY_HOOK`) is only scheduled while search engine updates are on, so the content audit batch and sitemap reads never run from cron otherwise; schedule it always (search updates still check their own setting).

## Files

`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php`, new `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-backlinks.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-collection.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-changes.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-api.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-cli.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-abilities.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-demo.php`, `includes/features/class-seoprostats-statistics.php`, `packages/core/src/types.ts`, `packages/core/src/state.ts`, new `packages/wp-admin/src/Backlinks.tsx`, `packages/wp-admin/src/Search.tsx`, `packages/wp-admin/src/api.ts`, `packages/wp-admin/src/labels.ts`, `docs/api/openapi.yaml`, `docs/architecture.md`, `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, `todo/PLANS.md`. body:

Uses the existing Search Console connection (`includes/stats/sources/class-seoprostats-source-search-console.php`, scope `webmasters.readonly`, which both APIs below accept). The Search Console API has no Links report (links come from #142, Bing and exports instead).

## What

- **Sitemaps** (`GET webmasters/v3/sites/{site}/sitemaps`): each submitted sitemap's path, type, last submitted, last downloaded, pending, errors and warnings, read daily by the import cron into a small option or table (`SEOProStats_Indexation` is the home). `contents[].indexed` is deprecated: do not show it. Search → Audit, Indexation shows a Sitemaps card: each sitemap with its state; errors or warnings, a sitemap Google has not downloaded in 7+ days, or WordPress's own sitemap index (`/wp-sitemap.xml`, or the SEO plugin's) not submitted at all become decision-queue items (`SEOProStats_Queue`) and Plan rows.
- **URL Inspection** (`POST https://searchconsole.googleapis.com/v1/urlInspection/index:inspect`, body `inspectionUrl`, `siteUrl`): the version in Google's index (not a live test). Budget: Google allows 2,000 a day and 600 a minute per property; use at most 200 a day by default (setting), from cron only, never on a visitor page. Order: the Indexation list's pages (never shown first), then pages with traffic whose last inspection is oldest; each page again after 14 days. Keep per page: verdict, coverageState, indexingState, robotsTxtState, pageFetchState, lastCrawlTime, googleCanonical vs userCanonical (a mismatch is a finding), crawledAs, rich results verdict and detected types with issues. New table `inspections` (schema bump: path_id primary key, checked key, the fields as codes and dictionary ids).
- **Reports**: Indexation rows gain Google's reason (coverage state) and last crawl; Audit gains findings "Google picked another canonical", "Blocked by robots.txt", "Crawled, not indexed", "Rich result errors". `GET /inspections` (filters: verdict, coverage), `wp seoprostats inspect [<page>] [--run]`, ability `seoprostats/inspections`, OpenAPI and core types. title: Backlinks from exports: Search Console Links and backlink tools' CSV into the links table
body:
Parent: #37 (outside data sources). Links from every source end up in one place: the `links` table from #142. Search Console has no links API, but its Links report exports CSV, and every backlink tool exports CSV; this issue reads those files.

## What

- **Import a links CSV** (Settings → Import → Links, `POST /backlinks/import` (multipart or JSON rows), `wp seoprostats backlinks import <file> [--source=<name>]`): detect the format by its header row:
  - Search Console → Links → External links → Export (latest links / more sample links: linking page, last crawled; top linking sites: site, linking pages, target pages).
  - Ahrefs, Semrush, Majestic, Moz and Bing Webmaster Tools backlink exports (referring page URL, target URL, anchor, nofollow / sponsored / ugc, first seen, last seen, authority score where given).
  - A generic CSV: source URL, target URL, anchor, rel, first seen.
  Rows to the site's own hosts only; each source gets its own `found` bit (Search Console export, other tool export); authority kept per provider where given (0-100). title: Link spam review and Google disavow file export
body:
Parent: #37 (outside data sources). Review backlinks from every existing source locally; nothing is sent anywhere.

## What

- Explain weighted spam signals per referring site, score 0–100: commercial/unrelated anchors (casino, pills, loans, adult terms kept in code), many links to many pages, fetched pages with hundreds of outgoing links, suspicious TLD patterns, differing language/script, provider spam score when supplied, redirect evidence when available, and links lost within days. Missing evidence must not be invented. Signals are review hints, not proof of spam.
- Search → Backlinks → Review: sites ordered by score, links, anchors and reasons. Per domain or source URL: keep (never flagged again), disavow, undecided; store who and when in an indexed link_reviews table. No automatic or external submission.

title: Research links: operator searches on Google, Bing, Brave and DuckDuckGo, and the Keyword Golden Ratio on targets
body:
Ref #37. Research shortcuts for the people choosing what to write: from any query or target, open the right searches on each engine, and judge a keyword with the Keyword Golden Ratio.

Facts: Google supports `site:`, `intitle:`, `allintitle:`, `inurl:`, `allinurl:`, `intext:`, `filetype:`, quotes, `-` and `OR`; some once-common operators are unreliable or retired (`cache:`, `related:`, `AROUND`, `daterange:`), so leave those out. Bing documents `site:`, `intitle:`, `inbody:`, `inanchor:`, `filetype:`, `contains:`, `language:`, `loc:`; Brave documents `site:`, `intitle:`, `inbody:`, `inpage:`, `filetype:`, quotes, `-` (marked experimental); DuckDuckGo documents `site:`, `intitle:`, `inurl:`, `filetype:`, quotes and `-` (may fall back to related results). Search URLs: verify each engine's query URL from its own documentation before use (DuckDuckGo's `https://duckduckgo.com/?q=` is documented).

The Keyword Golden Ratio (KGR): the number of Google results for `allintitle:<keyword>` divided by the keyword's monthly search volume, for keywords of at most 250 searches a month; under 0.25 is the target, 0.25 to 1 may work, over 1 is crowded. A heuristic, not a promise.

## What

- **Search links** on every query row (Search → Rankings queries, Opportunities, Targets, Coverage) and every target: a small menu "Research" with, per engine (Google, Bing, Brave, DuckDuckGo): the query; `allintitle:"query"`; `intitle:"query"`; `inurl:` the main word; `"query" -site:<site>` (competitors); `site:<site> "query"` (the site's own pages for it, to find cannibalisation and internal link sources); and for Google, `"query" intitle:forum OR inurl:forum` (questions people ask). Links open the engine in a new tab; nothing is fetched by the server (no scraping; engines forbid it). Templates kept in `packages/core` (portable), each with a short description.
- **KGR on targets**: Search → Targets gains columns allintitle results and monthly volume (entered by the owner, imported by CSV, or filled by a provider: DataForSEO search volume / SERP counts when #141 is connected, Bing keyword stats if its API offers them), the date each was taken, and the KGR with its band; sort and filter by KGR. The allintitle link above is next to the field, so the owner can read the count and type it in.
- REST/CLI/ability: targets answers gain `kgr`, `allintitle`, `volume`, `measured`; `wp seoprostats targets set <query> --allintitle=<n> --volume=<n>`.
- Docs: what each operator search is for, and KGR's limits.

## Files

`packages/core/src/research.ts` (new: templates and URL building), `packages/core/src/index.ts`, `packages/core/src/types.ts`, `packages/wp-admin/src/components/ResearchMenu.tsx` (new), `packages/wp-admin/src/Search.tsx`, `packages/wp-admin/src/Opportunities.tsx`, `packages/wp-admin/src/Targets.tsx`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-targets.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php` (targets columns), `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-api.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-cli.php`, `docs/api/openapi.yaml`, `docs/architecture.md`, `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`.

## Check

The menu's links open the expected searches on each engine (checked by opening them); a target with allintitle 40 and volume 200 shows KGR 0.2 in the good band; volume over 250 shows "volume too high for KGR". `npm run check`, `scripts/lint.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` pass; the menu works by keyboard, at 1440px and 390px.

title: Page experience from the Chrome UX Report (Core Web Vitals by page, against search traffic)
body:
Parent: #37 (outside data sources). Page experience from real Chrome users, so a slow page can be weighed against its search traffic and fixed where it matters most.

Facts: the Chrome UX Report (CrUX) API is free with a Google Cloud API key (150 queries a minute per project), gives origin and URL level field data (LCP, INP, CLS, FCP, TTFB as p75 and good/needs improvement/poor shares) over a rolling 28 days, updated daily; URLs without enough Chrome traffic have no record. The CrUX History API gives weekly history. PageSpeed Insights runs Lighthouse lab tests (key optional, recommended); Google is removing CrUX data from PSI, so field data comes from CrUX directly.

## What

- **Connection** (Settings → Connections → Chrome UX Report): an API key, stored encrypted like the other connections; a check request on the site's origin.
- **Daily read** (cron, budget): the origin (phone and desktop), then the site's top pages by visits and search clicks (default 100, setting), each URL at most weekly; history for the origin from the History API on connect. New table `vitals` (schema bump: day, path_id (0 origin), form factor, metric, p75, good/ni/poor shares; primary key on them; key path_day).
- **Reports**: Search → Audit gains "Page experience": pages failing Core Web Vitals (any of LCP, INP, CLS poor at p75), ordered by search clicks and visits; Overview/Search charts can show the origin's p75 per metric; a change `vitals_status` (group site) when the origin or a top page moves between good, needs improvement and poor, so it lines up with traffic. Decision-queue items for failing pages with search traffic.
- Optional, owner-triggered only: a Lighthouse run (PSI API) for one page from its row, showing the main opportunities.
- REST `GET /vitals`, `wp seoprostats vitals [<page>] [--run]`, ability `seoprostats/vitals`, OpenAPI, core types, demo data, docs.

title: IndexNow: notify search engines of published, changed and removed pages
body:
Ref #37. Tell search engines at once when a page is published, changed or removed, so new and fixed pages are crawled sooner, and show what was sent next to the changes it followed.

Facts: IndexNow (indexnow.org) is a change notification, not analytics: the site hosts a key file (`/<key>.txt` holding the key), then POSTs up to 10,000 URLs per request to a participating endpoint; participating engines share submissions; HTTP 200 means received, not indexed. Google does not take part. Bing's Webmaster API also has URL submission with a daily quota (see the Bing site data issue).

## What

- **Setting** (Settings → Data, off by default): "Notify search engines of changed pages (IndexNow)", with what is sent (only the page addresses) and to whom.
- **Key**: generated on first use, served at `/<key>.txt` by a rewrite (no file write needed), kept in an option.
- **When**: the change log already sees published, unpublished, address, title, content and SEO field changes (`SEOProStats_Changes`); those pages are queued and sent in one POST by cron within a minute (deduplicated, at most once per page per hour), never on a visitor request. Unpublished or moved pages send the old address too.
- **Record**: each submission (time, count, answer code) in a small option log (last 100), and the change rows get `meta.indexnow` (sent, code), so the timeline shows it. Errors (403 key not valid, 422, 429) shown on the connection card.
- `wp seoprostats indexnow [status|send <url>...]`, REST `GET /indexnow`, docs.

## Files

`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-indexnow.php` (new), `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-changes.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-collection.php` (cron), `includes/features/class-seoprostats-statistics.php` (setting), `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-api.php`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-cli.php`, `uninstall.php`, `docs/architecture.md`, `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`.

## Check

On a public test site: the key URL answers with the key; publishing a post sends one request with its URL and a 200/202 is recorded; editing it twice within the hour sends once. Setting off: nothing is sent and the key URL answers 404. `scripts/lint.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` pass (no query or request on visitor pages).

title: Launch sweep: security findings (filter escaping, hashes, workflows, dev dependencies)
body:
Part of #160 (launch sweep, security first).

## Real bug: filter values ending in a backslash

CodeQL `js/incomplete-sanitization` at `packages/core/src/filters.ts:27`. `serializeFilter()` escapes `,` as `\,` but not `\`, so the values `a\` and `b` serialize to `a\,b`, which reads back as the one value `a,b`. The PHP reader has the same gap: `SEOProStats_Query` (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-query.php`, around line 205) splits on `(?<!\\),`.

Fix: `\\` is a backslash and `\,` a comma in a value (any other backslash stays as written, so existing links keep working). Write `\` as `\\` before `,` as `\,` in `serializeFilter()`; read both escapes in `splitValues()` and in the PHP reader (a character scan instead of the lookbehind). Document `\\` in `docs/api/openapi.yaml` next to `\,` (around line 2862).

## Explained or marked, not changed

- `md5()` as a cache key, row fingerprint or demo ID (SonarCloud php:S4790, Codacy weak-crypto): `class-seoprostats-query.php`, `-changes.php`, `-ab-report.php`, `-ab-tests.php`, `-search-updates.php`, `-demo.php`. Inline `// NOSONAR nosemgrep: <reason>` per `STANDARDS.md` → Code.
- `http://` in `SEOProStats_Migrate_Matomo::address()`: builds an address only to read its path; inline reason.
- `http://` to the loopback Docker site in `scripts/demo-site.sh` and `scripts/shop-test.sh`, `exec()` with `escapeshellarg()` in `scripts/replaced-plugins.php`, the digits-only include path and HMAC echo in `collect.php`, fixed-key jQuery selectors in `admin/js/seoprostats-admin.js`, the escaped glob in `packages/tracker/src/index.ts`, the literal regex in `Plan.tsx`, the same-origin REST URL in `packages/wp-admin/src/api.ts`: marked as false positives in SonarCloud/Codacy with the reason.

## Workflows (Scorecard, SonarCloud githubactions:S7637)

`.github/workflows/star-history.yml` (added by the aidevops badge sync, not a starter core file): pin `star-history-reusable.yml` and `aidevops_ref` to the commit `repo-metrics.yml` uses (v3.38.4), top-level `contents: read`, `contents: write` on the job only. `release.yml` and `repo-metrics.yml` need their job-level write; dismiss those two Scorecard alerts as "won't fix" with the reason.

## Dependabot (development dependencies only)

Bring the 7 alerts' packages to fixed versions (`npm update` in range; `overrides` in `package.json` for transitive ones), then `npm run build` and `scripts/lint.sh` must still pass.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `scripts/lint.sh`; CI required checks.
- A filter with values `a\` and `b` round-trips through `serializeFilter`/`parseFilter`, and the REST API returns the same rows for `?filters=page:is:a\\,b` as the two values.
- After merge: CodeQL alert 15 closed, Dependabot open alerts 0, SonarCloud vulnerabilities 0.

title: Code smells: PHP statistics classes (nested ternaries, repeated strings, small rules)
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

Parent: #160 (public-launch sweep → Code smells by area). Findings on `main` at `fb407fb`: 102 (SonarCloud 98, Codacy PHP Mess Detector 4).

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `seoprostats code smells sonar cognitive complexity refactor` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 open PRs in wpallstars/seoprostats; last merges on these files were #164, #166, #168 (findings fetched after them)
- [x] File refs verified: 25 files from SonarCloud/Codacy at `fb407fb`, all present at HEAD
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — Rule-by-rule patterns are known; keep-or-fix choices for callbacks and demo data need judgment.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — findings list is the starting context; fixes need per-site judgment

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-09, interactive session (ai-interactive), public-launch sweep #160.
- **Conversation context:** Codacy and SonarCloud settings now fit the code (ESLint/PHPMD config files, `assets/build/` excluded); the remaining findings are real smells, filed as small pull requests by area (`DEVELOPMENT.md` → At public launch, step 2).

## What

The SonarCloud and Codacy code smells in `includes/stats/class-*.php` other than complexity and class size are fixed or kept with an inline reason: nested ternaries, repeated string literals, `switch` without `default`, mergeable `if`s, loop-counter changes, duplicated regex characters and similar. The five most complex classes (CLI, processor, query, inspections, changes) are a separate issue. Behaviour, REST responses, WP-CLI output and stored data are unchanged.

## Why

The repository is public and its SonarCloud and Codacy badges show these counts. `DEVELOPMENT.md` step 2: every finding is fixed, explained in an inline comment, or marked a false positive with the reason (`STANDARDS.md` → Code: `// NOSONAR: <reason>` on that line only).

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Rule-by-rule patterns are known; keep-or-fix choices for callbacks and demo data need judgment.

## PR Conventions

Leaf issue: the PR resolves this issue and refers to the parent with `For #160`.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `STANDARDS.md` → Code (inline reasons, NOSONAR form) and the finding table below.
- **Load only if:** `docs/architecture.md` when a change touches collection, storage, reports, REST or WP-CLI.
- **Stop when:** each listed finding is fixed or has its reason.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: includes/stats/class-seoprostats-ab-report.php` — php:S3358, php:S2234
- `EDIT: includes/stats/class-seoprostats-ab-tests.php` — php:S3358 ×3
- `EDIT: includes/stats/class-seoprostats-api.php` — php:S1192, php:S1066
- `EDIT: includes/stats/class-seoprostats-audit.php` — php:S1192, php:S3358, php:S131

- `EDIT: includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search-updates.php` — php:S3358 ×2
- `EDIT: includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search.php` — php:S3358 ×5, php:S1192 ×2
- `EDIT: includes/stats/class-seoprostats-shares.php` — php:S3358

- `EDIT: includes/stats/class-seoprostats-ua.php` — rulesets-naming.xml-ShortMethodName
- `EDIT: changelog.txt` — one `= Unreleased =` line: `* Developers: ... (GH#160).`

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** the listed files' existing callers; no public function, method, hook, REST route or WP-CLI command changes name or signature (`rg -n '<name>' includes packages` before renaming anything private).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** N/A because no write path changes: database writes (`$wpdb->insert`/`query` in `includes/stats/`), options and transients keep their SQL, keys and order.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `scripts/lint.sh` (PHP syntax, phpcs, PHPStan level 8, TypeScript check, build must match `assets/build/`); `scripts/smoke-test.sh` in CI (pages, admin screens, WP-CLI, query EXPLAIN, uninstall).
- **Schemas/config:** none; `docs/api/openapi.yaml` unchanged.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** none: these files are not built (`assets/build/` comes from `packages/`).
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because no stored data or table changes (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php` untouched).
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `git revert` of the PR; N/A for data because no settings, rows or files are written differently.

### Implementation Steps

1. Nested ternaries (`php:S3358`): `if`/`elseif` or a `match`-free lookup array (PHP 7.4 is the minimum: no `match`). Repeated literals (`php:S1192`, most in `class-seoprostats-demo.php`, the demo-data generator): a private class constant where the string means one thing; demo URLs and labels that are data, not names, may stay with `// NOSONAR: demo data` on the first line. Unused parameters (`php:S1172`) in hook, WP-CLI or field-type callbacks must stay (WordPress passes them): add `// NOSONAR: <hook> passes it`. `php:S107` (too many parameters) and `php:S1479` (too many cases) may be kept with a reason when splitting would only move the list. Translated strings stay literal for `__()`. Run `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` after each file.
2. Keep a finding only with an inline reason on that line (`// NOSONAR: <reason>` for SonarCloud; `@SuppressWarnings("PHPMD.<Rule>")` with a reason for PHPMD; `// eslint-disable-next-line <rule> -- <reason>`).
3. Run `scripts/lint.sh` and fix anything it reports before pushing.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** no change: refactors keep the order of database writes and locks.
- **Migration/rollback:** none; a revert restores the old code with no data impact.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** PHP 7.4 and WordPress 6.2 stay the minimums (no `match`, no PHP 8-only syntax); public PHP and REST interfaces keep their signatures.
- **Idempotency/retry:** unchanged behaviour; WP-CLI and cron jobs produce the same results when re-run.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** unchanged; error paths keep returning the same `WP_Error` codes and messages.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash scripts/lint.sh
curl -s 'https://sonarcloud.io/api/issues/search?componentKeys=wpallstars_seoprostats&types=CODE_SMELL&resolved=false&ps=1&branch=main' | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["total"])'
```

- **Surface mapping:** `scripts/lint.sh` proves syntax, coding standards, PHPStan, types and build parity for every listed file; CI's smoke tests prove pages, admin screens, WP-CLI and query plans; the SonarCloud count (after merge, on `main`) proves the findings are gone.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required beyond the required CI checks.

title: Code smells: PHP outside the statistics classes (collector, migration adapters, sources, admin tabs)
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

Parent: #160 (public-launch sweep → Code smells by area). Findings on `main` at `fb407fb`: 13 (SonarCloud 12, Codacy Opengrep 1).

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `seoprostats code smells sonar cognitive complexity refactor` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 open PRs in wpallstars/seoprostats; last merges on these files were #164, #166, #168 (findings fetched after them)
- [x] File refs verified: 9 files from SonarCloud/Codacy at `fb407fb`, all present at HEAD
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — Known patterns; the collector's tainted-filename finding needs a security judgment on the path's origin.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — findings list is the starting context; fixes need per-site judgment

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-09, interactive session (ai-interactive), public-launch sweep #160.
- **Conversation context:** Codacy and SonarCloud settings now fit the code (ESLint/PHPMD config files, `assets/build/` excluded); the remaining findings are real smells, filed as small pull requests by area (`DEVELOPMENT.md` → At public launch, step 2).

## What

The SonarCloud and Codacy code smells in the plugin's own PHP outside `includes/stats/class-*.php` are fixed or kept with an inline reason: the collector (`collect.php`), migration adapters (`includes/stats/migrate/`), search sources, admin tabs and test scripts. Behaviour is unchanged; the collector still loads no WordPress and makes no extra file or database calls (`AGENTS.md` → Visitor pages pay nothing).

## Why

The repository is public and its SonarCloud and Codacy badges show these counts. `DEVELOPMENT.md` step 2: every finding is fixed, explained in an inline comment, or marked a false positive with the reason (`STANDARDS.md` → Code: `// NOSONAR: <reason>` on that line only).

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Known patterns; the collector's tainted-filename finding needs a security judgment on the path's origin.

## PR Conventions

Leaf issue: the PR resolves this issue and refers to the parent with `For #160`.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `STANDARDS.md` → Code (inline reasons, NOSONAR form) and the finding table below.
- **Load only if:** `docs/architecture.md` when a change touches collection, storage, reports, REST or WP-CLI.
- **Stop when:** each listed finding is fixed or has its reason.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: collect.php` — Semgrep_php.lang.security.injection.tainted-filename.tainted-filename
- `EDIT: includes/admin/class-seoprostats-connections-tab.php` — php:S1192
- `EDIT: includes/admin/class-seoprostats-dashboard.php` — php:S1192 ×2
- `EDIT: includes/stats/migrate/class-seoprostats-migrate-jetpack.php` — php:S3358
- `EDIT: includes/stats/migrate/class-seoprostats-migrate-koko.php` — php:S3358
- `EDIT: includes/stats/migrate/class-seoprostats-migrate-matomo.php` — php:S1192, php:S3358
- `EDIT: includes/stats/migrate/class-seoprostats-migrate-slimstat.php` — php:S3358
- `EDIT: includes/stats/sources/class-seoprostats-source-search-console.php` — php:S3358 ×2
- `EDIT: scripts/shop-test-mu.php` — php:S1192 ×2
- `EDIT: changelog.txt` — one `= Unreleased =` line: `* Developers: ... (GH#160).`

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** the listed files' existing callers; no public function, method, hook, REST route or WP-CLI command changes name or signature (`rg -n '<name>' includes packages` before renaming anything private).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** N/A because no write path changes: database writes (`$wpdb->insert`/`query` in `includes/stats/`), options and transients keep their SQL, keys and order.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `scripts/lint.sh` (PHP syntax, phpcs, PHPStan level 8, TypeScript check, build must match `assets/build/`); `scripts/smoke-test.sh` in CI (pages, admin screens, WP-CLI, query EXPLAIN, uninstall).
- **Schemas/config:** none; `docs/api/openapi.yaml` unchanged.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** none: these files are not built (`assets/build/` comes from `packages/`).
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because no stored data or table changes (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php` untouched).
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `git revert` of the PR; N/A for data because no settings, rows or files are written differently.

### Implementation Steps

1. Nested ternaries (`php:S3358`): `if`/`elseif` or a lookup array (PHP 7.4 minimum). Repeated literals (`php:S1192`): a private class constant when the string means one thing. `collect.php` tainted-filename (Codacy Opengrep): check the path is built only from the plugin's own constants and a validated site ID; if so, add `// nosemgrep: <reason>` on that line, matching the existing reasons from #162 (`rg -n nosemgrep collect.php includes`); if any part comes from the request unvalidated, validate it. Migration adapters read other plugins' data only (`AGENTS.md` → Other plugins' data is read only): change no query that touches their tables beyond its PHP shape. Run `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` after each file.
2. Keep a finding only with an inline reason on that line (`// NOSONAR: <reason>` for SonarCloud; `@SuppressWarnings("PHPMD.<Rule>")` with a reason for PHPMD; `// eslint-disable-next-line <rule> -- <reason>`).
3. Run `scripts/lint.sh` and fix anything it reports before pushing.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** no change: refactors keep the order of database writes and locks.
- **Migration/rollback:** none; a revert restores the old code with no data impact.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** PHP 7.4 and WordPress 6.2 stay the minimums (no `match`, no PHP 8-only syntax); public PHP and REST interfaces keep their signatures.
- **Idempotency/retry:** unchanged behaviour; WP-CLI and cron jobs produce the same results when re-run.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** unchanged; error paths keep returning the same `WP_Error` codes and messages.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash scripts/lint.sh
curl -s 'https://sonarcloud.io/api/issues/search?componentKeys=wpallstars_seoprostats&types=CODE_SMELL&resolved=false&ps=1&branch=main' | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["total"])'
```

- **Surface mapping:** `scripts/lint.sh` proves syntax, coding standards, PHPStan, types and build parity for every listed file; CI's smoke tests prove pages, admin screens, WP-CLI and query plans; the SonarCloud count (after merge, on `main`) proves the findings are gone.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required beyond the required CI checks.

### Files Scope

- `collect.php`
- `includes/admin/class-seoprostats-connections-tab.php`
- `includes/admin/class-seoprostats-dashboard.php`
- `includes/stats/migrate/class-seoprostats-migrate-jetpack.php`
- `includes/stats/migrate/class-seoprostats-migrate-koko.php`
- `includes/stats/migrate/class-seoprostats-migrate-matomo.php`
- `includes/stats/migrate/class-seoprostats-migrate-slimstat.php`
- `includes/stats/sources/class-seoprostats-source-search-console.php`
- `scripts/shop-test-mu.php`
- `changelog.txt`

1. CSS: one declaration per line where a block has several (`declaration-block-single-line-max-declarations`), modern colour and alpha notation (`rgb(0 0 0 / 50%)`), and blank lines before comments and rules. title: Code smells: split the most complex PHP functions (CLI, processor, query, inspections, changes)
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

Parent: #160 (public-launch sweep → Code smells by area). Findings on `main` at `fb407fb`: 208 (SonarCloud 109, Codacy PHP Mess Detector 99).

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `seoprostats code smells sonar cognitive complexity refactor` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 open PRs in wpallstars/seoprostats; last merges on these files were #164, #166, #168 (findings fetched after them)
- [x] File refs verified: 5 files from SonarCloud/Codacy at `fb407fb`, all present at HEAD
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — Behaviour-preserving decomposition of large, query-heavy functions needs design judgment on helper boundaries and on what to leave as a flat list.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — findings list is the starting context; fixes need per-site judgment

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-09, interactive session (ai-interactive), public-launch sweep #160.
- **Conversation context:** Codacy and SonarCloud settings now fit the code (ESLint/PHPMD config files, `assets/build/` excluded); the remaining findings are real smells, filed as small pull requests by area (`DEVELOPMENT.md` → At public launch, step 2).

## What

The five PHP files with the most cognitive-complexity findings have their long functions split into named private helpers, so each function does one thing: SonarCloud `php:S3776` (cognitive complexity over 15) and PHP Mess Detector's cyclomatic and NPath complexity drop for these files. Behaviour is unchanged: same WP-CLI output, REST responses, stored rows and query plans.

## Why

The repository is public and its SonarCloud and Codacy badges show these counts. `DEVELOPMENT.md` step 2: every finding is fixed, explained in an inline comment, or marked a false positive with the reason (`STANDARDS.md` → Code: `// NOSONAR: <reason>` on that line only).

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** Behaviour-preserving decomposition of large, query-heavy functions needs design judgment on helper boundaries and on what to leave as a flat list.

## PR Conventions

Leaf issue: the PR resolves this issue and refers to the parent with `For #160`.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `STANDARDS.md` → Code (inline reasons, NOSONAR form) and the finding table below.
- **Load only if:** `docs/architecture.md` when a change touches collection, storage, reports, REST or WP-CLI.
- **Stop when:** each listed finding is fixed or has its reason.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: includes/stats/class-seoprostats-changes.php` — rulesets-codesize.xml-CyclomaticComplexity ×11, php:S3358 ×10, rulesets-codesize.xml-NPathComplexity ×9, php:S3776 ×7, rulesets-codesize.xml-ExcessiveClassComplexity, rulesets-codesize.xml-ExcessiveClassLength, rulesets-codesize.xml-TooManyMethods, rulesets-codesize.xml-TooManyPublicMethods, php:S1448, php:S1172, rulesets-codesize.xml-ExcessiveMethodLength, php:S1479
- `EDIT: includes/stats/class-seoprostats-cli.php` — php:S3776 ×20, php:S3358 ×7, php:S1172 ×6, php:S1192 ×6, php:S1448, php:S6353, php:S138
- `EDIT: includes/stats/class-seoprostats-inspections.php` — rulesets-codesize.xml-CyclomaticComplexity ×10, rulesets-codesize.xml-NPathComplexity ×8, php:S3776 ×8, php:S131 ×4, rulesets-codesize.xml-ExcessiveClassComplexity, rulesets-codesize.xml-ExcessiveClassLength, rulesets-codesize.xml-TooManyMethods, rulesets-codesize.xml-TooManyPublicMethods, rulesets-design.xml-CouplingBetweenObjects, php:S1448, php:S1192
- `EDIT: includes/stats/class-seoprostats-processor.php` — rulesets-codesize.xml-CyclomaticComplexity ×15, php:S3776 ×11, rulesets-codesize.xml-NPathComplexity ×8, rulesets-codesize.xml-ExcessiveMethodLength ×2, php:S3358 ×2, rulesets-codesize.xml-ExcessiveClassComplexity, rulesets-codesize.xml-ExcessiveClassLength, rulesets-codesize.xml-TooManyMethods, php:S1448, php:S1192, php:S5869, rulesets-naming.xml-ShortMethodName
- `EDIT: includes/stats/class-seoprostats-query.php` — rulesets-codesize.xml-CyclomaticComplexity ×10, php:S3776 ×9, rulesets-codesize.xml-NPathComplexity ×7, php:S1192 ×3, php:S3358 ×3, rulesets-codesize.xml-ExcessiveClassComplexity, rulesets-codesize.xml-ExcessiveClassLength, rulesets-codesize.xml-TooManyMethods, rulesets-codesize.xml-TooManyPublicMethods, php:S1448, php:S127, rulesets-codesize.xml-ExcessiveMethodLength
- `EDIT: changelog.txt` — one `= Unreleased =` line: `* Developers: ... (GH#160).`

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** the listed files' existing callers; no public function, method, hook, REST route or WP-CLI command changes name or signature (`rg -n '<name>' includes packages` before renaming anything private).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** N/A because no write path changes: database writes (`$wpdb->insert`/`query` in `includes/stats/`), options and transients keep their SQL, keys and order.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `scripts/lint.sh` (PHP syntax, phpcs, PHPStan level 8, TypeScript check, build must match `assets/build/`); `scripts/smoke-test.sh` in CI (pages, admin screens, WP-CLI, query EXPLAIN, uninstall).
- **Schemas/config:** none; `docs/api/openapi.yaml` unchanged.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** none: these files are not built (`assets/build/` comes from `packages/`).
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because no stored data or table changes (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php` untouched).
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `git revert` of the PR; N/A for data because no settings, rows or files are written differently.

### Implementation Steps

1. Decide per function whether to split: extract steps into private static helpers named for what they do (argument parsing, validation, row building, formatting), keeping each helper's inputs explicit. Do not change public method signatures, hook names, option names, SQL or the order of side effects. `class-seoprostats-cli.php`: one helper per subcommand step; WP-CLI `$args`/`$assoc_args` handling stays in the command method. `class-seoprostats-processor.php` and `class-seoprostats-query.php`: keep every query and its index use exactly as is (the smoke test EXPLAINs them). Where a function is long because it is a flat list (a schema, a field map), keep it and add `// NOSONAR: a flat list, not logic` instead. One commit per file. The table also lists these files' smaller findings (nested ternaries, repeated literals, `switch` without `default`; patterns as in the other PHP smell issue: lookup arrays or `if`/`elseif`, private constants, `// NOSONAR: <hook> passes it` for callback parameters WordPress passes); fix them in the same pass so no other worker edits these files. Other files' complexity findings are a later step of #160, once this shows the pattern.
2. Keep a finding only with an inline reason on that line (`// NOSONAR: <reason>` for SonarCloud; `@SuppressWarnings("PHPMD.<Rule>")` with a reason for PHPMD; `// eslint-disable-next-line <rule> -- <reason>`).
3. Run `scripts/lint.sh` and fix anything it reports before pushing.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** no change: refactors keep the order of database writes and locks.
- **Migration/rollback:** none; a revert restores the old code with no data impact.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** PHP 7.4 and WordPress 6.2 stay the minimums (no `match`, no PHP 8-only syntax); public PHP and REST interfaces keep their signatures.
- **Idempotency/retry:** unchanged behaviour; WP-CLI and cron jobs produce the same results when re-run.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** unchanged; error paths keep returning the same `WP_Error` codes and messages.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash scripts/lint.sh
curl -s 'https://sonarcloud.io/api/issues/search?componentKeys=wpallstars_seoprostats&types=CODE_SMELL&resolved=false&ps=1&branch=main' | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["total"])'
```

- **Surface mapping:** `scripts/lint.sh` proves syntax, coding standards, PHPStan, types and build parity for every listed file; CI's smoke tests prove pages, admin screens, WP-CLI and query plans; the SonarCloud count (after merge, on `main`) proves the findings are gone.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required beyond the required CI checks.

### Files Scope

- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-changes.php`
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-cli.php`
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-inspections.php`
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-processor.php`
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-query.php`
- `changelog.txt`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every finding in the table below is fixed or has an inline reason; after merge, SonarCloud and Codacy show none of them open on `main`.
- [ ] `scripts/lint.sh` passes and the required CI checks (Lint, Release build, both Smoke tests) pass.
- [ ] No behaviour change: no public function, hook, REST route, WP-CLI command or stored-data format is renamed or changed, and no new PHP warnings appear in the smoke test's debug log.

## Findings

Rules: `php:S3776` 55, `rulesets-codesize.xml-CyclomaticComplexity` 46, `rulesets-codesize.xml-NPathComplexity` 32, `php:S3358` 22, `php:S1192` 11, `php:S1172` 7, `php:S1448` 5, `php:S131` 4, `rulesets-codesize.xml-ExcessiveMethodLength` 4, `rulesets-codesize.xml-ExcessiveClassLength` 4, `rulesets-codesize.xml-TooManyMethods` 4, `rulesets-codesize.xml-ExcessiveClassComplexity` 4, `rulesets-codesize.xml-TooManyPublicMethods` 3, `php:S127` 1, `php:S138` 1, `php:S6353` 1, `php:S1479` 1, `php:S5869` 1, `rulesets-design.xml-CouplingBetweenObjects` 1, `rulesets-naming.xml-ShortMethodName` 1.

The SonarCloud and Codacy code smells in `packages/wp-admin/src` other than read-only props and cognitive complexity are fixed, or kept with an inline reason: nested ternaries become `if`/early returns, small lookup objects or helper functions; optional chaining, `Set`/`includes`, `startsWith` and similar suggestions are applied where they keep behaviour. Rendered screens are unchanged.

## Why

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `STANDARDS.md` → Code (inline reasons, NOSONAR form) and the finding table below.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** the listed files' existing callers; no public function, method, hook, REST route or WP-CLI command changes name or signature (`rg -n '<name>' includes packages` before renaming anything private).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** N/A because no write path changes: database writes (`$wpdb->insert`/`query` in `includes/stats/`), options and transients keep their SQL, keys and order.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `scripts/lint.sh` (PHP syntax, phpcs, PHPStan level 8, TypeScript check, build must match `assets/build/`); `scripts/smoke-test.sh` in CI (pages, admin screens, WP-CLI, query EXPLAIN, uninstall).
- **Schemas/config:** none; `docs/api/openapi.yaml` unchanged.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `assets/build/` is committed build output: rebuild with `npm run build` and commit it.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because no stored data or table changes (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php` untouched).
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `git revert` of the PR; N/A for data because no settings, rows or files are written differently.

### Implementation Steps

1. Work file by file from the table. Nested ternaries (`typescript:S3358`, most in `Plan.tsx`): extract a small function returning the value, or a lookup object keyed by state; keep JSX readable. `typescript:S6819` (use a native element instead of a `role`): switch to `<button>`/`<table>` only when styling and keyboard behaviour stay the same, otherwise keep and add `// NOSONAR: <reason>`. `no-stringify-keys` (Codacy Opengrep): `JSON.stringify()` used as a cache or dependency key is intended when the object is built in a fixed key order; say so in a one-line comment, or build the key from the fields. Rebuild with `npm run build` and commit `assets/build/`.
2. Keep a finding only with an inline reason on that line (`// NOSONAR: <reason>` for SonarCloud; `@SuppressWarnings("PHPMD.<Rule>")` with a reason for PHPMD; `// eslint-disable-next-line <rule> -- <reason>`).
3. Run `scripts/lint.sh` and fix anything it reports before pushing.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** no change: refactors keep the order of database writes and locks.
- **Migration/rollback:** none; a revert restores the old code with no data impact.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** PHP 7.4 and WordPress 6.2 stay the minimums (no `match`, no PHP 8-only syntax); public PHP and REST interfaces keep their signatures.
- **Idempotency/retry:** unchanged behaviour; WP-CLI and cron jobs produce the same results when re-run.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** unchanged; error paths keep returning the same `WP_Error` codes and messages.

```bash
curl -s 'https://sonarcloud.io/api/issues/search?componentKeys=wpallstars_seoprostats&types=CODE_SMELL&resolved=false&ps=1&branch=main' | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["total"])'
```

- **Surface mapping:** `scripts/lint.sh` proves syntax, coding standards, PHPStan, types and build parity for every listed file; CI's smoke tests prove pages, admin screens, WP-CLI and query plans; the SonarCloud count (after merge, on `main`) proves the findings are gone.

title: Code smells: tracker, core and charts packages
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

Parent: #160 (public-launch sweep → Code smells by area). Findings on `main` at `fb407fb`: 35 (SonarCloud 35).

blocked-by:#175 — `core` and `charts` are bundled into the same built files (`assets/build/dashboard.js` and others) that #175 rebuilds; start after it merges, from fresh `main`.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `seoprostats code smells sonar cognitive complexity refactor` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 open PRs in wpallstars/seoprostats; last merges on these files were #164, #166, #168 (findings fetched after them)
- [x] File refs verified: 6 files from SonarCloud/Codacy at `fb407fb`, all present at HEAD
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — Small set, but the tracker's size and browser-support constraint needs judgment per finding.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — findings list is the starting context; fixes need per-site judgment

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-09, interactive session (ai-interactive), public-launch sweep #160.
- **Conversation context:** Codacy and SonarCloud settings now fit the code (ESLint/PHPMD config files, `assets/build/` excluded); the remaining findings are real smells, filed as small pull requests by area (`DEVELOPMENT.md` → At public launch, step 2).
- **Blocked by:** #175 (same built files).

## What

The SonarCloud and Codacy code smells in `packages/tracker`, `packages/core` and `packages/charts` are fixed or kept with an inline reason, without growing the tracker or changing its requests.

## Why

The repository is public and its SonarCloud and Codacy badges show these counts. `DEVELOPMENT.md` step 2: every finding is fixed, explained in an inline comment, or marked a false positive with the reason (`STANDARDS.md` → Code: `// NOSONAR: <reason>` on that line only).

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Small set, but the tracker's size and browser-support constraint needs judgment per finding.

## PR Conventions

Leaf issue: the PR resolves this issue and refers to the parent with `For #160`.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `STANDARDS.md` → Code (inline reasons, NOSONAR form) and the finding table below.
- **Load only if:** `docs/architecture.md` when a change touches collection, storage, reports, REST or WP-CLI.
- **Stop when:** each listed finding is fixed or has its reason.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: packages/charts/src/markers.ts` — typescript:S7765, typescript:S4624, typescript:S7768
- `EDIT: packages/charts/src/timeseries.ts` — typescript:S7773, typescript:S6582
- `EDIT: packages/core/src/coverage.ts` — typescript:S7773 ×2, typescript:S6353, typescript:S6557, typescript:S8786
- `EDIT: packages/core/src/filters.ts` — typescript:S7780
- `EDIT: packages/core/src/state.ts` — typescript:S6582, typescript:S4624
- `EDIT: packages/tracker/src/index.ts` — typescript:S6582 ×5, typescript:S7765 ×3, typescript:S6557 ×3, typescript:S6606 ×2, typescript:S7761 ×2, typescript:S3358 ×2, typescript:S5843, typescript:S7780, typescript:S6551, typescript:S7773, typescript:S8786
- `EDIT: assets/build/ab-test.asset.php` — rebuilt by `npm run build` if a source above changes it
- `EDIT: assets/build/ab-test.js` — rebuilt by `npm run build` if a source above changes it
- `EDIT: assets/build/dashboard.asset.php` — rebuilt by `npm run build` if a source above changes it
- `EDIT: assets/build/dashboard.js` — rebuilt by `npm run build` if a source above changes it
- `EDIT: assets/build/editor.asset.php` — rebuilt by `npm run build` if a source above changes it
- `EDIT: assets/build/editor.js` — rebuilt by `npm run build` if a source above changes it
- `EDIT: assets/build/share.asset.php` — rebuilt by `npm run build` if a source above changes it
- `EDIT: assets/build/share.js` — rebuilt by `npm run build` if a source above changes it
- `EDIT: assets/build/tracker.js` — rebuilt by `npm run build` if a source above changes it
- `EDIT: assets/build/widget.asset.php` — rebuilt by `npm run build` if a source above changes it
- `EDIT: assets/build/widget.js` — rebuilt by `npm run build` if a source above changes it
- `EDIT: changelog.txt` — one `= Unreleased =` line: `* Developers: ... (GH#160).`

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** the listed files' existing callers; no public function, method, hook, REST route or WP-CLI command changes name or signature (`rg -n '<name>' includes packages` before renaming anything private).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** N/A because no write path changes: database writes (`$wpdb->insert`/`query` in `includes/stats/`), options and transients keep their SQL, keys and order.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `scripts/lint.sh` (PHP syntax, phpcs, PHPStan level 8, TypeScript check, build must match `assets/build/`); `scripts/smoke-test.sh` in CI (pages, admin screens, WP-CLI, query EXPLAIN, uninstall).
- **Schemas/config:** none; `docs/api/openapi.yaml` unchanged.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `assets/build/` is committed build output: rebuild with `npm run build` and commit it.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because no stored data or table changes (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php` untouched).
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `git revert` of the PR; N/A for data because no settings, rows or files are written differently.

### Implementation Steps

1. The tracker (`packages/tracker/src/index.ts`) runs on every visitor page and must stay tiny and work in old browsers it supports today: do not add syntax the build does not already emit (check `assets/build/tracker.js` size before and after; it must not grow by more than a few bytes). Prefer `// NOSONAR: <reason>` there when a suggestion (optional chaining, `String.raw`, `dataset`) would grow the output or change browser support. In `core` and `charts`, apply the suggestion when behaviour is the same. These packages stay free of WordPress and React (`AGENTS.md` → Portable underneath). Rebuild with `npm run build` and commit `assets/build/`.
2. Keep a finding only with an inline reason on that line (`// NOSONAR: <reason>` for SonarCloud; `@SuppressWarnings("PHPMD.<Rule>")` with a reason for PHPMD; `// eslint-disable-next-line <rule> -- <reason>`).
3. Run `scripts/lint.sh` and fix anything it reports before pushing.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** no change: refactors keep the order of database writes and locks.
- **Migration/rollback:** none; a revert restores the old code with no data impact.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** PHP 7.4 and WordPress 6.2 stay the minimums (no `match`, no PHP 8-only syntax); public PHP and REST interfaces keep their signatures.
- **Idempotency/retry:** unchanged behaviour; WP-CLI and cron jobs produce the same results when re-run.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** unchanged; error paths keep returning the same `WP_Error` codes and messages.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash scripts/lint.sh
curl -s 'https://sonarcloud.io/api/issues/search?componentKeys=wpallstars_seoprostats&types=CODE_SMELL&resolved=false&ps=1&branch=main' | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["total"])'
```

- **Surface mapping:** `scripts/lint.sh` proves syntax, coding standards, PHPStan, types and build parity for every listed file; CI's smoke tests prove pages, admin screens, WP-CLI and query plans; the SonarCloud count (after merge, on `main`) proves the findings are gone.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required beyond the required CI checks.

### Files Scope

- `packages/charts/src/markers.ts`
- `packages/charts/src/timeseries.ts`
- `packages/core/src/coverage.ts`
- `packages/core/src/filters.ts`
- `packages/core/src/state.ts`
- `packages/tracker/src/index.ts`
- `changelog.txt`
- `assets/build/ab-test.asset.php`
- `assets/build/ab-test.js`

- `assets/build/dashboard.js`
- `assets/build/editor.asset.php`
- `assets/build/editor.js`

- `assets/build/share.js`

- `assets/build/widget.js`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every finding in the table below is fixed or has an inline reason; after merge, SonarCloud and Codacy show none of them open on `main`.
- [ ] `scripts/lint.sh` passes and the required CI checks (Lint, Release build, both Smoke tests) pass.

title: Sortable columns on search tables: impressions first by default, second click reverses
body:
## What

Search → Rankings → Top searches: every metric column (Clicks, Impressions, CTR, Position) sorts the table. Queries and pages (and the other top-search kinds) default to Impressions, most first. Days keep newest first by default, and their Day column sorts too.

Sorting: the first click on a column sorts its natural way (most first for clicks, impressions, CTR, visits and conversions; lowest first for position; newest first for days); a second click on the active column reverses it.

The same applies to the other tables of pages with these search figures:

- Search → Content (Clicks and Visits from search sort today, most first only): add Impressions, make the figure columns sortable both ways, default Impressions.
- Search → Audit (pages, most impressions first): Impressions, Clicks, CTR and Position sortable both ways.

## How

- Server: `sort` + `order` (`asc`|`desc`, default the column's natural direction) on `GET /search`, `GET /content`, `GET /audit`, the matching WP-CLI commands and abilities; `docs/api/openapi.yaml`.
  - `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search.php` `rows()` `ORDER BY`; `day_rows()` sorts the points.
  - `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-content.php` `order()`; `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-audit.php` `build()` `usort`.
- Core: `packages/core/src/types.ts` sort keys per report; `packages/core/src/state.ts` keeps `sort` + `order` in the address.
- wp-admin: one shared sortable header (pattern: `PageTable` in `packages/wp-admin/src/Content.tsx`), used by `Search.tsx`, `Content.tsx` and `Audit.tsx`.
- `DESIGN.md` sortable header rule: ↓/↑ for the direction, `aria-sort` ascending/descending.

## Verification

- Build, typecheck, lint and PHP lint clean.
- REST: `/search?kind=queries&sort=position&order=asc`, `/content?sort=impressions`, `/audit?sort=ctr` return rows in that order.
- wp-admin: click a header twice; the order reverses, the arrow flips, and the address keeps it.

The purpose-ranked tables (Opportunities, Targets, Links) get a follow-up once this lands.

title: shop-test.sh: doctor's unscheduled daily cron aborts the test before its last checks
body:
## What happens

`scripts/shop-test.sh` stops with `Error: 1 check failed.` on a clean run, after every shop check has printed PASS. This happens on v1.1.0 and on the 1.2.0 release branch, on both WordPress latest / PHP 8.2 and WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4.

## Cause

`check_results()` (`scripts/shop-test.sh`, around line 282) runs:

```bash
doctor="$(wp_cli seoprostats doctor --format=json --quiet)"
```

On the disposable site, `doctor` reports one failed check:

```json
{"check":"cron seoprostats_daily","status":"fail","detail":"not scheduled (an admin page schedules it)"}
```

The test site never loads an admin page, so the daily event is never scheduled. `doctor` then exits non-zero (`SEOProStats_CLI::doctor()`, `WP_CLI::error()` when any check is `fail`). The script runs under `set -euo pipefail`, so the failed command substitution exits before the ThriveCart doctor assertion and the PHP log check, and those checks never run.

Seen while preparing 1.2.0, using a temporary copy of the script that prints the doctor checks whose status is not `ok`. The purchase totals, visit joins and PHP log all passed.

## Fix

In `scripts/shop-test.sh`, schedule the plugin's cron events the way an admin page would before calling `doctor`, or read the JSON without letting the exit code abort the script. Then assert only the `purchases` check, as it does today. Keep `doctor`'s exit code for any check the test actually cares about; do not hide real failures.
